info.title: Trellis API
info.description: Launch surface: a router runs LAUNCH_SURFACE=core by default and then serves only the operations marked `x-launch-surface: core` in this document (chat completions, completions, embeddings, models, keys, prepaid credits, wallet sign-in, x402 per call, generations and receipts, attestation, status). Every other operation answers 404 `not_enabled` (components.responses.NotEnabled) on such a router; `GET /api/v1/status` reports the surface under `data.launch_surface`. Scope: a documented subset of the public HTTP API that the Trellis router implements. It covers the model catalog, chat completions, embeddings, key creation and listing, generations, status, health and receipts, plus the blind-token issuer keys and purchase (present only when the router enables blind tokens) the Oblivious HTTP gateway keys, gateway and relay list (present only when the router enables Oblivious HTTP) the transparency log of keys and configurations with its tiles, checkpoints and witness cosignatures (present only when the router enables it) the Lane: model variants, day-zero candidates and creator royalty claims, Private RAG (answers from documents sent with the question, nothing kept), and the Batch API (many chat or embeddings requests run in the background, with the lines and answers kept sealed outside the database until the results expire). It also covers teams as pseudonymous organisations: roles, passkey and wallet (Solana) members, org budgets and the hash-chained audit log with its export, and characters: Tavern cards called as @character/<id>, with a memory ledger encrypted on the client. It also covers prepaid USDC credits on Solana (deposit transactions, account closure, spend-only balances), wallet sign-in, the hosted x402 facilitator (schemes exact and tab), the Harvest Index and $TRLS holder tiers (membership levels that give access and priority, never a price change: the tier table, early access to newly listed models and advisory polls). Other implemented routes (for example legacy completions, the /v1 aliases, key updates, BYOK, rankings and provider onboarding) are not described here, and a route's absence from this document does not mean it is absent from the router. Endpoint availability, payment modes and model capabilities are deployment-specific. Errors share the OpenRouter-shaped ApiError body; the 4xx responses each operation can return are declared with the reusable responses in components.responses. Chain: Solana; amounts are USDC (6 decimals); addresses are base58 ed25519 public keys and transaction references are base58 signatures. Payment headers: X-PAYMENT / PAYMENT-SIGNATURE (x402 exact), X-Trellis-Tab and X-Trellis-Tab-Voucher (the tab scheme), X-Pay-With (pay with a tokenized stock), X-Wallet-Auth (a wallet spending its change or an operator view).

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Optional signed account event notices; WEBHOOK_SIGNING_ENABLED defaults to false.

tags.name: Data tools
tags.description: Read-only market data for agents, charged per call: Stock Token prices from Chainlink feeds on Solana, corporate-action (multiplier) status and the inference price index. DATA_TOOLS_ENABLED defaults to false; every route answers 404 data_tools_disabled while it is off. A refusal (unknown symbol, stale feed, paused token, index without fills) is answered before any payment and is never charged.

tags.name: Agent rulebook
tags.description: Deterministic router enforcement for requests through Trellis only; AGENT_POLICY_ENABLED defaults to false. No on-chain enforcement.

tags.name: Playbooks
tags.description: One named rulebook that many keys of an account or team follow; a change applies to every following key from its next request. Same switch, roles and validation as the agent rulebook: AGENT_POLICY_ENABLED defaults to false.

tags.name: Network host policy
tags.description: Versioned signed build pins for future network host admission; existing provider admission is unchanged.

tags.name: Models
tags.description: Public model catalog and capabilities.

tags.name: Chat
tags.description: Chat completion requests and streaming responses.

tags.name: Embeddings
tags.description: Authenticated prepaid embedding requests.

tags.name: Keys
tags.description: API key creation and account key metadata.

tags.name: Generations
tags.description: Authenticated generation summaries and details.

tags.name: Status
tags.description: Public process and router configuration status.

tags.name: Receipts
tags.description: Public signed receipt retrieval and verification.

tags.name: Saved Routes
tags.description: Named routing policies callable as model @route/<slug>.

tags.name: Presets
tags.description: Versioned configs callable as model @preset/<name> or @preset/<name>@<version>: a saved route plus a system prompt, tools and a response_format, with diff and rollback.

tags.name: Agent Sessions
tags.description: Short-lived, budget-capped session keys for agent runs.

tags.name: Spend Watch
tags.description: Spend reports, key budgets and alert rules.

tags.name: MCP
tags.description: Remote Model Context Protocol server: every live model as a tool.

tags.name: Anthropic Messages
tags.description: Anthropic Messages API (POST /v1/messages, count_tokens) for the Anthropic SDKs and Claude Code, on the same keys, lanes and signed receipts as chat completions.

tags.name: Blind tokens
tags.description: Unlinkable paid access with Privacy Pass tokens (RFC 9578 type 0x0002, blind RSA per RFC 9474). Present only when the router enables blind tokens.

tags.name: Oblivious HTTP
tags.description: Oblivious HTTP gateway (RFC 9458) and the relays that reach it, behind the unlinkable lane. Present only when the router enables Oblivious HTTP.

tags.name: Disclosure
tags.description: What each provider has documented about how it handles a prompt (retention, jurisdiction, legal hold, training use), and the request options that route on it.

tags.name: Lane
tags.description: Model variants (mainstream, native_low_refusal, abliterated) with license and weights provenance, the rule that keeps restricted variants on attested providers, and the operator's day-zero candidate pipeline.

tags.name: Creator royalties
tags.description: Claim a model's creator royalty by publishing a challenge in the Hugging Face repository the weights come from.

tags.name: Responses
tags.description: OpenAI Responses API compatible endpoint for the OpenAI Agents SDK, the Codex CLI and other Responses clients. Stateless: nothing is stored.

tags.name: Private RAG
tags.description: Answers from documents sent with the question, ranked in memory and kept nowhere, through the router's own embeddings and chat routes.

tags.name: Transparency log
tags.description: An append-only log (C2SP tlog-tiles, RFC 6962 hashing) of the keys and configurations clients encrypt to or verify against: receipt keys, Oblivious HTTP key configurations, blind-token issuer keys, measurement bundles and sidecar key bindings. Checkpoints are signed notes (C2SP tlog-checkpoint) that witnesses cosign (C2SP tlog-cosignature, cosignature/v1). With TLOG_REKOR_ENABLED, each new checkpoint is also recorded in Sigstore's Rekor log (a hashedrekord entry signed with an ECDSA P-256 anchoring key), an alternative to witnesses. Present only when the router enables it (TLOG_ENABLED).

tags.name: Ollama
tags.description: The Ollama API under /ollama for Ollama clients (Open WebUI, Continue, the ollama libraries, LangChain's ChatOllama): set the client's host to <router>/ollama. Chat, generate and embed calls run on the same keys, lanes and signed receipts as chat completions; the key is sent as Authorization: Bearer.

tags.name: Batches
tags.description: The Batch API: many chat completions or embeddings requests sent in one call and run in the background on the router's worker, with results kept for 24 hours after the batch finishes. A line costs what the same call costs: BATCH_DISCOUNT_BPS is 0 by default. Not on the core launch surface.

tags.name: Rerank
tags.description: Rerank documents against a query (Cohere and Jina shape), billed per token or per search unit, with a signed receipt.

tags.name: Teams
tags.description: Anonymous organisations: an owner that is an account or a Solana wallet (base58 address, ed25519 signature over the router's challenge message; a multisig vault cannot sign a message and is not bindable yet), members who join by passkey or wallet, roles (owner, admin, dev, viewer, agent), an org budget, and a hash-chained audit log you can export and verify offline.

tags.name: Status page
tags.description: The public status page: availability, latency and error budgets per privacy lane and API surface, and incidents with Atom and RSS feeds. The public lane is summed from request outcomes; the attested and unlinkable lanes come only from the differentially private hourly releases at /api/v1/stats (source: dp-noised).

tags.name: Characters
tags.description: Tavern character cards (V2 and V3, as JSON or PNG) called as model @character/<id>: public, unlisted or private (encrypted on the client), with a chat endpoint that defaults to the attested lane, group turn order and creator attribution (counts and cost only).

tags.name: Memory
tags.description: A memory ledger for characters, encrypted on the client: the router stores ciphertext under a scope it cannot link to a character, and embeddings only when the caller opts in.

tags.name: Skills
tags.description: Secured Skills Hub for agent skills (a folder with SKILL.md and its scripts and resources): import from a git repository or an archive, a static scan for data exfiltration, prompt injection, obfuscation, dangerous shell commands, untrusted package indexes and binaries, a sha256 content hash of a canonical tar, gated downloads and paid installs (90% to the author, 10% network fee) with a signed receipt. Scanned, not guaranteed.

tags.name: Paid tools
tags.description: Pay any x402 tool priced in USDC on Solana from a Trellis balance: rulebook price limits, holds, signed tool.call receipts, a listing catalog with daily known-answer canaries, and MCP tools trellis_tools_search and trellis_tools_call. Off unless TOOLS_MARKET_ENABLED.

tags.name: Agent identity
tags.description: Portable agent identity for opted-in agent profiles (an ERC-8004-shaped registration file served by the router; no identity registry is deployed on Solana yet), paid-receipt feedback, liveness probes and portable track records. Off by default.

tags.name: Credits
tags.description: Prepaid USDC credits on Solana (program trellis_credits): deposits are spend-only; the only outflows are fair-fail refunds, account-closure refunds and settlement to hosts. Deposits move USDC from the payer's wallet into the program vault under the key's hash; balances are credited once the transaction is finalized.

tags.name: Wallet sign-in
tags.description: Sign in with a Solana wallet: a server-issued single-use challenge, an ed25519 signature by the wallet's key, and a management key for the wallet's account (w_<address>), the same account a per-call x402 payer's change is kept on.

tags.name: Facilitator
tags.description: The hosted x402 facilitator (docs §5.2) for schemes exact and tab on Solana (solana:5eykt4UsFv8P8NJdTREpY1vzqKqZKvdp; devnet when the router runs there). Non-custodial: funds move payer to payee; the relay key only co-signs as fee payer. The facilitator charges no fee. Request and answer shapes follow Coinbase's facilitator so any x402 seller library can point at this URL. Present only when the router enables it (data.facilitator.enabled in GET /api/v1/status).

tags.name: HVX
tags.description: The Harvest Index: the public hourly $/1M-token price of sealed open-model inference per grade (G-S, G-M, G-L), built from paid receipts with self-dealing and circular volume excluded. Public, read-only, cached a minute.

tags.name: Holder tiers
tags.description: $TRLS holder tiers: the tier table, the tier of the wallet behind a key, early access to newly listed models, and advisory polls. Holder tiers are membership levels with fixed thresholds. Their perks are access and priority only; no tier changes a price, and every caller pays the host's price. Describes current behaviour, which can change. Present only when the router sets thresholds (data.enabled in GET /api/v1/holders/tiers); no thresholds are set by default.

get.summary: Preview an approval's ask-first amount change
get.description: B118: management or same-team owner/admin auth as Approve. Inference and session keys refused. Only amount-only approvals for the current own rulebook; playbook followers return 409 playbook_linked with playbook_id and playbook_name. AGENT_POLICY_ENABLED false returns 404; actions require AGENT_GUARD_ENABLED. Returns data.field, before_usd, after_usd, amount_usd and policy_sha256. Preview changes nothing.

200.description: Exact threshold change; amounts are decimal USD strings.

409.description: Not pending, not amount-only, rules changed or playbook followed

post.summary: Approve and allow next time
post.description: B118: same auth and eligibility as GET. In one transaction approves once and saves only approval.above_usd for model calls or actions.approval_above_usd for actions, rounded up to the cent, with the schema version and hash-chained policy_set and approval_approved events. Caps are unchanged. Original single-use retry binding and expiry remain. Changed hash returns 409. Telegram unchanged.

200.description: data contains approval (existing approval shape), change (the GET preview), policy (updated rulebook), version (schema version) and sha256 (new policy digest).

409.description: Not pending, not amount-only, rules changed or playbook followed

get.description: V87: STATEMENTS_ENABLED defaults false; disabled route returns 404. Management and owner/admin keys see the account; ordinary and session keys see only their own attributed movements labelled scope=key. Exact USDC decimal strings reconcile to the ledger in one snapshot: opening + deposits + refunds - usage - separate fees + other changes = closing. Usage groups reconcile to usage. UTC month; usage by settlement time, calls by generation time. Current month is so_far. Months before account creation and future months return 404. Holds, external payments and embedded usage fees are not added to totals. Canonical payload JSON is signed with the existing receipt Ed25519 key and key_id; verify with published receipt keys. Print the account-shell HTML view for PDF. No new storage.

sig.description: Base64 signature of canonical payload JSON

payload.description: trellis.statement.v1: month, currency, UTC bounds, generated_at, account_created_at, scope, key_hash, opening_balance, deposits, refunds, usage, fees, other_changes, closing_balance, calls, usage_by_model, usage_by_key_agent, usage_by_lane, movements_by_kind, reconciliation, limits. Money and calls are decimal strings. Group ids can be null.

get.description: V6 R: MAKEGOOD_ENABLED defaults to false; the route returns 404 while it is off (GET /api/v1/status reports makegood.enabled). Deterministic refunds decided from facts recorded when a call is served or fails: upstream_failure (a per-call payment for a request no provider served, 100%, on-chain), fallback_price (failover to a pricier provider, the price difference), truncated_stream (billed output tokens never delivered), structured_output (the JSON repair answer still does not parse, 100% of the repair call) and unattested_lane (100% plus a host strike). Capped by what the ledger charged; at most one refund per call or payment. Management and owner/admin keys see the account, other keys their own calls; a per-call wallet payer can read its refunds with X-Wallet-Auth signed for this GET (the request path with its query string, and the hash of the empty body). Each issued refund has a signed v1 receipt of kind refund at GET /api/v1/receipts/{id} naming original_receipt_id. Cache-Control: no-store.

WEBHOOK_SIGNING_ENABLED defaults to false; switched on at trellis.example. Requires owner/admin access outside agent sessions. Account-wide destinations require a management key; other callers manage only linked destinations scoped to their own key. Secrets appear only on creation or rotation. All responses use Cache-Control: no-store. See /docs/#signed-webhooks for exact-byte HMAC verification, five-minute timestamp tolerance, signed event_id binding and durable duplicate suppression. Delivery can repeat after a crash. Activity discovery has bounded source-retention limits. Approval and operated host status writers queue references atomically. Direct database writes do not create those notices.

get.description: Calls (with receipt ids and verify links), agent approvals and rule decisions, alerts, deposits and balance changes, and agreement events, newest first, in one item shape with exact USDC amounts. A key sees its own activity; management, owner and admin keys see the account within their team boundaries. format=csv returns this page as CSV with X-Next-Cursor when another page exists.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: call, approval, alert, deposit, agreement, policy, balance or topup

get.description: Pending approvals with their expiry, alerts, deposits, key auto top-ups, agreement events and status updates for hosts the account operates, under the same access rules as /api/v1/activity. Pass since (the seen time the browser keeps) to mark newer items. B119: when LOW_BALANCE_ALERTS_ENABLED is true, account-scope inboxes also include low-balance crossings with kind low_balance, id, at, title, amount (decimal USD balance), status null, href /dashboard/#money, and unread. Session and ordinary key-scope inboxes cannot see these account alerts.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: ISO 8601 seen time, not in the future

post.summary: Return a seen time for the displayed inbox
post.description: Validates the key and returns the seen time to keep in the browser. Nothing is stored on the server.

parameters.name: through
parameters.description: ISO 8601 time of the displayed snapshot, not in the future

get.description: Present only with NETWORK_STATS_ENABLED (default false). Public read-only snapshots cached at most 30 seconds; HTTP freshness is limited to remaining snapshot lifetime. Host counts include only network hosts. Attested capacity requires fresh successful hardware attestation and admission evidence. Public-lane token ranges use 100,000-token buckets, not differential privacy, from retained generation records only. Private-lane host totals are unavailable: existing DP counters have no host dimension or 7/30-day history. Null means absent records or a disabled optional source. Bond amounts retain index freshness. Waitlist counts express interest only.

503.description: Aggregate source unavailable; no stale response is served

get.description: Management key or owner/admin of the target key’s account and team, with the same permissions as editing that key. Includes effective rulebooks, kill state, rolling spend plus reservations and caps. Off returns 404.

stopped_until.description: B117: Optional timed stop deadline; alerts retain the deadline captured at the stop and include it in webhook and Telegram delivery.

get.description: Includes own and inherited parent rulebooks, remaining rolling caps and kill state. Optional autonomy reports rung, since, clean_requests, last_clean_at, caps_multiplier and next (rung, after_days, clean_requests, caps_multiplier, elapsed_days, days_remaining, requests_remaining), or null at the top. effective_caps scales only spending caps. Progress resets on selected deny, kill or recorded breaker events and on rulebook saves. A session and its parent must both pass. Off returns 404.

stopped_until.description: B117: Effective timed stop deadline; omitted when running or any stopped inherited policy has no deadline. Also reported by MCP trellis_agent_rules. Each timed policy in policies reports its own deadline.

409.description: Approval is no longer pending

get.description: AGENT_POLICY_ENABLED defaults false; off returns 404. Management key or same-account team owner/admin. Up to 100 newest rows. Pending by default. Expiry ends validity but does not delete approval rows.

409.description: Approval is no longer pending

get.description: Principal or the requesting key; returns only id, status and expires_at. Off returns 404.

409.description: Approval is no longer pending

post.summary: Approve a pending approval
post.description: Management key or same-account team owner/admin of the requesting key. Session and ordinary agent keys cannot decide. Records the principal key hash and a chained event. Expired or completed rows return 409. Off returns 404. Retry inference with X-Agent-Approval: <id> after approval; it is single-use, binds key/model/lane/tools/output token limit, and permits estimated cost no greater than the approved ceiling. All rulebook restrictions still apply. AGENT_APPROVAL_TTL_S defaults to 900 seconds from request time.

409.description: Approval is no longer pending

post.summary: Deny a pending approval
post.description: Management key or same-account team owner/admin of the requesting key. Session and ordinary agent keys cannot decide. Records the principal key hash and a chained event. Expired or completed rows return 409. Off returns 404. Retry inference with X-Agent-Approval: <id> after approval; it is single-use, binds key/model/lane/tools/output token limit, and permits estimated cost no greater than the approved ceiling. All rulebook restrictions still apply. AGENT_APPROVAL_TTL_S defaults to 900 seconds from request time.

post.summary: Evaluate an Intent without recording it
post.description: Calling API key. Returns a deterministic decision with no event writes or automatic kill. Off returns 404.

get.description: Management key or owner/admin of the target key’s account and team, with the same permissions as editing that key. Off returns 404.

put.description: Management key or owner/admin of the target key’s account and team, with the same permissions as editing that key. Replaces the specification while preserving existing kill state. Off returns 404.

delete.description: Management key or owner/admin of the target key’s account and team, with the same permissions as editing that key. Removes this key’s own rulebook; a session’s inherited parent rulebook still applies. Off returns 404.

get.description: Management key, or a team owner or admin; viewers, devs, agent keys and session keys are refused. A management key sees every playbook of the account; a team owner or admin sees its team's and the account-wide ones. Each lists how many keys follow it and the following keys the caller manages. Off (AGENT_POLICY_ENABLED false) returns 404.

post.summary: Create a playbook
post.description: Management key, or a team owner or admin; viewers, devs, agent keys and session keys are refused. A team owner or admin creates a playbook for its own team; a management key creates an account-wide one, or one for a team it owns with team_id. Version starts at 1. Off (AGENT_POLICY_ENABLED false) returns 404.

409.description: playbook_name_taken or playbook_limit_reached

get.description: Management key, or a team owner or admin; viewers, devs, agent keys and session keys are refused. Adds the latest 50 recorded changes, newest first. Off (AGENT_POLICY_ENABLED false) returns 404.

put.description: Management key, or a team owner or admin; viewers, devs, agent keys and session keys are refused. Account-wide playbooks change only with a management key. New rules raise version by one and are copied, in the same transaction, to every key that follows the playbook, which uses them from its next request. Unchanged name and rules change nothing (changed false). For a team the change is in the team audit log, and a change of rules is in the inbox of the team's owners and admins. Off (AGENT_POLICY_ENABLED false) returns 404.

409.description: playbook_name_taken

delete.description: Management key, or a team owner or admin; viewers, devs, agent keys and session keys are refused. Refused with 409 playbook_followed and metadata.followers while keys follow the playbook, unless unlink=copy: each following key then keeps the playbook's rules as its own rulebook. Off (AGENT_POLICY_ENABLED false) returns 404.

409.description: playbook_followed

post.summary: Follow a playbook, or stop following
post.description: Management key or owner/admin of the target key's account and team, with the same permissions as editing that key. With a playbook_id, the key's rules become that playbook's current rules (its stop state is kept); a team playbook takes keys of that team only (409 playbook_team_mismatch). With null, the key stops following and keeps the playbook's current rules as its own. While a key follows a playbook, PUT and DELETE on its own rulebook answer 409 playbook_linked. Off (AGENT_POLICY_ENABLED false) returns 404.

409.description: playbook_team_mismatch

post.summary: Stop an agent
post.description: Management key or owner/admin of the target key’s account and team, with the same permissions as editing that key. A committed kill is read on the next request by every replica, without policy caching. Requires an existing rulebook. Off returns 404.

until.description: B117: Optional ISO time with timezone, future and at most 30 days ahead; omitted stops until manual Resume. The next enforcement check after expiry clears the stop atomically and appends a resume event with reason scheduled.

post.summary: Resume an agent
post.description: Management key or owner/admin of the target key’s account and team, with the same permissions as editing that key. Clears kill state without changing the specification. Off returns 404.

post.summary: Replay a draft rulebook on the last days of recorded activity
post.description: Same permissions as setting that key’s rulebook. Evaluates the draft against up to 5,000 of the key’s recorded calls (its own and its session keys’: model, lane, cost, tokens and time, never the text) and Agent Guard checks in the window, oldest first, with running caps, calls per hour, windows, breakers, autonomy and Stop. Read only: nothing is saved, charged or changed. Ten a minute per calling key. What the record cannot tell is listed in notes. Off returns 404.

get.description: Management key or owner/admin of the target key’s account and team, with the same permissions as editing that key. Newest first, 50 per page. next_cursor is a before-id cursor. Metadata-only hash chain; 90-day retention when the cleanup worker runs. Off returns 404.

post.summary: Apply or re-apply a network host using existing wallet authentication
post.description: Available only with NETWORK_HOSTS_ENABLED=true; default false. See /docs/#network-host-signup. post.summary: Create a chat completion
post.description: Supports standard JSON responses and Server-Sent Events when stream is true. A model must support requested capabilities such as tools or response_format. Auth may use a bearer key, wallet authentication, or the per-call payment flow. A 402 response can contain a quote; follow its payment instructions before retrying the exact request. When the router has x402 enabled, the 402 body is also an x402 v1 payment requirement (x402Version, accepts) and the PAYMENT-REQUIRED header carries the same requirement as x402 v2: build the exact-scheme USDC TransferChecked transaction with extra.feePayer as fee payer, sign it as the payer and retry with X-PAYMENT (v1) or PAYMENT-SIGNATURE (v2); the facilitator co-signs and submits it and the paid response carries the settlement in X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE and PAYMENT-RESPONSE. Change stays on the payer's wallet account and can be spent with X-Wallet-Auth. A tab (the tab x402 scheme) pays instead with X-Trellis-Tab and X-Trellis-Tab-Voucher: the payer's session key signs a cumulative voucher per request and the escrowed cap settles on close. X-Pay-With names a tokenized-stock mint to pay with instead of USDC credits. If that answer is lost, the same request with the same payment and a PAYMENT-RECOVERY signature gets the kept answer again, byte for byte, without a second payment. Two opt-in modes run several billed calls for one request and are off unless the router enables them: model trellis/council (a panel of models plus a judge; see the council field) and verify "dual" (the same request to two providers; see the verification field). Both are non-streaming only. Where the router enables blind tokens, Authorization: PrivateToken token=<base64url> pays with one token instead of a key (see the Blind tokens tag): the call is charged to a pooled account, the signed receipt carries the token's nullifier and no payer, and the token is spent only if the call is served. A token pays for at most its value, so a request whose worst case costs more is refused with 402 token_value_too_low; council mode and verify are refused with 400 blind_unsupported. A refused, unknown, expired or already spent token is a 401 that carries WWW-Authenticate: PrivateToken challenge="...". Disclosure ceilings and lanes apply to token calls exactly as to key calls. Lane unlinkable, where the router enables Oblivious HTTP, is served only for a request that arrives through the gateway (POST /api/v1/ohttp/gateway) by way of an independent relay, paid with a blind token and never a key, and only by attested providers; where the router serves the lane over Tor (data.lanes.unlinkable.via in GET /api/v1/status includes onion), a request that arrives through its onion service (data.onion.url) and is paid with a blind token qualifies in the same way, streamed or not, and a clearnet request cannot claim to have come that way; otherwise it is refused with 403 lane_requires_anonymous_auth for an API key or a wallet (unless provider.lane_downgrade is attested, which serves it on lane attested instead), 403 unlinkable_requires_relay or unlinkable_requires_independent_relay, 401 unlinkable_requires_token with the token challenge when no token is presented, or 503 no_attested_endpoint when no attested endpoint can serve the model. A request that arrives through an independent relay, is paid with a blind token and names no lane is served on lane unlinkable. On lanes attested and unlinkable the router never falls back to an endpoint without a fresh, verified attestation: it answers 503 no_attested_endpoint instead. Within a lane endpoints are weighted uptime x quality x attested_bonus / price^2 (attested_bonus 1.25 on public, 1 elsewhere). On attested and unlinkable the router still terminates TLS and sees the prompt; end-to-end encryption through the router is planned. Through the gateway, streaming needs chunked Oblivious HTTP (message/ohttp-chunked-req), where the router enables it; stream true in a message/ohttp-req is refused with 400 stream_unsupported. Holds: before a call is sent the router holds its worst case, which is a bound and not an estimate. Prompt tokens are bounded by the UTF-8 bytes of the text (non-ASCII text counts the larger of its bytes and its NFKD-normalised bytes; characters are never divided by a ratio), plus fixed template allowances (64 tokens per request, 16 per message, 256 when tools or functions are present); every other forwarded field that is a string, array or object (tools, functions, response_format, stop, tool calls, unknown fields) counts the bytes of its indented JSON. Top-level numbers and booleans, model, stream, stream_options and router-only fields are not counted. The same bound is used for the context check and for a key's tokens-per-minute limit. Image, audio, video and file parts count the per-item token limit the model's catalog entry declares (input_token_limits in GET /api/v1/models); such input to a model that declares none, an unknown content-part type, a provider-side tool (a tools entry whose type is not function) and web_search_options are refused with 400 unboundable_input. An explicit output cap is always sent to the provider: max_tokens (and max_completion_tokens when the caller sent it) is the smallest of the caller's value, the catalog's output limit for the model (16,384 when the catalog has none) and the room the context leaves after the prompt bound. A higher value is clamped, not refused, and an omitted value is filled in; the same holds for council members, the judge and dual verification. The hold is the prompt bound at the dearest input price the model lists (the prompt price, or the cache write or read price if dearer), plus the output cap for every completion asked for (n) at the dearer of the completion and reasoning price, plus the per-request price per completion and the per-image price per image. The caller is charged at most the hold, always: when a provider reports usage priced above it, the charge stays at the hold, usage.cost_details.over_hold (number) and the receipt's cost_details.over_hold (USD string) carry the list price of the reported usage, and the provider is paid no more than the caller was charged. When a provider reports no usage at all, prompt tokens are billed at a third of the bound and marked estimated. A hold is renewed while its request is in flight; one that expired mid-request is still charged when the request settles, capped at the hold. top_logprobs must be an integer from 0 to 20 (400 invalid_request).

post.summary: Verify a signed receipt
post.description: A v1 receipt (payload, sig, key_id) is checked as before. A v2 receipt is sent as cose (the COSE_Sign1 bytes, base64) and is checked in order: signature, then request_sha256 and response_sha256 when given, then the chunk hash chain when chunks (the data of every streamed event before the receipt, in order) are given, then the anchor path. The result reports each step (signature_valid, hashes_valid, chain_valid, inclusion_valid; null when not run) and valid is false when any step that ran failed. Either form also reports decision_tag, the X-Trellis-Decision-Tag the receipt carries (null when none), and, when the request includes decision_tag (the SHA-256 of your order), decision_tag_valid; a mismatch makes valid false. Decision tags are recorded only while DECISION_TAGS_ENABLED is on. When an anchor with an index is given, onchain_status says what the router found on chain for that anchor of its own: verified (the root is there: a finalized transaction, signed by the router's anchorer key, in time, with no earlier root of that key for the hour, or the anchor program's account), unverified (it is not, or what is there does not verify), not_posted, or unknown (the chain was not consulted: the RPC failed, or this caller's budget of chain lookups for the minute is used up; no further RPC work is done then). onchain_root is set only when onchain_status is verified. valid covers the signature and the Merkle path and does not by itself say the root is on chain. The anchor mode, the program and the anchorer keys used here are the router's own configuration; nothing about them is read from the request.

With format=cose the COSE_Sign1 bytes themselves are returned (application/cose), or as base64 text with encoding=base64; 404 when the receipt has no v2 encoding. The response also carries privacy, the plain-English privacy label computed from the payload (see GET /api/v1/receipts/{id}/privacy); it is added beside the signed fields and is not signed. A make-good refund id (rf_...) returns its signed v1 refund receipt (kind refund, naming original_receipt_id) in the same shape, without v2 or anchor.

get.summary: Merkle path to the hourly root
get.description: Public. Once the receipt's hour has been rooted, the sorted-pair sha256 Merkle path from the receipt's leaf (the v2 leaf when it has one; v=1 selects the v1 leaf, which sits in the same tree) to the root. Before that, rooted is false. anchored is true only when the root was posted to the trellis_anchor program on Solana and confirmed; a router without a configured chain keeps the root off chain (status local) and says anchored false. status is confirmed, pending, local, late or conflict. In memo mode (mode memo: the root is a line signed by the router's anchorer key in an SPL Memo transaction, given as memo) a root is confirmed only once its transaction is finalized; late means it landed after the lateness bound and is not an anchor; conflict means the anchorer key had already signed another root for the hour, so this one was not posted; both say anchored false. An hour without receipts still gets a line (count 0). mode, contract, network, anchorer and memo tell a verifier what to look for on chain; which mode, network, program and anchorer keys to trust it takes from its own configuration (see /.well-known/trellis-receipt-keys.json), never from this answer.

The router reads every prompt in memory to route it on every lane, and the label says so. A field the receipt does not carry is reported as not recorded, never assumed; on an unlinkable receipt the address is reported hidden only because that lane is served solely to requests that arrive over Tor (or an independent relay). The label does not verify the receipt: check its signature with POST /api/v1/receipts/verify or the client library, which also computes the same label with privacyLabel(receipt). The same object is returned as `privacy` by GET /api/v1/receipts/{id}, beside the signed payload and never inside it.

With ANCHOR_MODE=memo the root is posted as a memo line signed by the router's anchorer key (mode memo, memo, anchorer, network): status is confirmed only once that transaction is finalized, late when it landed after the lateness bound, conflict when the anchorer key had already signed another root for the host and hour; late and conflict say anchored false. A receipt is checked by canonicalizing its payload (keys sorted, no whitespace), verifying the signature with the key whose kid is the receipt's key_id, and confirming the kid is the first 16 hex characters of SHA-256 of the raw key. The same list is served at /api/v1/receipts/keys. Beside keys, anchor says where receipt roots are posted: mode (memo or program), network (the cluster's CAIP-2 id), program (program mode), memo_program, anchorer and anchorers (the anchorer keys, oldest first, each with from_hour and the rotation_tx in which the key before it and the new key signed the hand-over), memo_v2_from_hour (memo mode: root lines of this hour and later are trellis:root:v2 lines, which name the transaction of the previous root; earlier hours have v1 lines) and max_late_seconds (memo mode: how long after its hour closed a root may land and still count). The document is not signed. get.summary: Proof-time: how long each attesting provider has held a fresh attestation
get.description: Public. For every live or shadow provider that has a TEE and an attestation endpoint: the current status (by the same rule as GET /api/v1/attestation/{providerId}), and the share of the last 24 hours and 7 days in which the router held a fresh attestation it verified itself. A fresh attestation is one the router verified at most fresh_within_ms ago (three attestor intervals) with no failed run since; a failed run, or evidence accepted only as simulated, ends the cover at once. share is the covered part of the time the record spans (observed_ms); when the record does not reach back to the start of the window (history_complete false) the earlier time is unknown and counts neither way, and share is null when nothing is recorded. buckets divides the window into equal slices, each the percent covered, or null before the record begins. Also: measurement changes in the last 7 days, the last measurement change (which fields, from and to), the last failed check as a code with a fixed message (never the provider's own text), the pass rate of the last 7 days' checks, and the latest health-probe and canary outcomes. Nothing here is raw provider output. Returns 501 not_enabled when the router keeps no history (ATTESTATION_HISTORY_DAYS is 0).

501.description: not_enabled: this router keeps no attestation history.

get.summary: A provider's recorded attestation, canary and probe events
get.description: Public. Newest first. Each event is one attestor run (kind attestation: ok or a failure code, the report hash, the TLS pin's SPKI hash when pinned, the verifiers that accepted the quote, the digests the run reported and whether they differ from the previous run's), one canary run (kind canary), or a change of the health probe's outcome (kind probe; only changes are recorded). Events are kept for history_days. Page with before set to the previous page's next: it encodes the moment and id of the last event, so events at the same instant are neither skipped nor repeated. Returns 404 for an unknown provider and 501 not_enabled when the router keeps no history.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: The next value of the previous page.

parameters.name: ok
parameters.description: Only events that passed (true) or failed (false).

501.description: not_enabled: this router keeps no attestation history.

get.summary: The key measurement bundles must be signed with
get.description: Public; 404 until the router is configured with a measurement key. A measurement bundle names the compose hash, source commit and tarball hash, model digest and image digests of a provider's attested software, with an MRTD and RTMR3 allow-list. It counts only if it is signed with this ECDSA P-256 key (SHA-256, DER signature over the bundle's canonical JSON) and the entry recording it in the transparency log verifies. key_id is the SHA-256 of the SubjectPublicKeyInfo.

get.summary: A provider's signed measurement bundles and their transparency-log entries
get.description: Public; 404 until the router is configured with a measurement key. Newest first. Each item carries the bundle, its signature and digest, the status the router reached (pending, verified or rejected, with the reason), the log entry it verified (uuid, index, integration time, whether the inclusion proof, checkpoint signature and signed entry timestamp verified) and, once verified, the log's own copy of the entry (entry_record: body, inclusion proof, signed entry timestamp) so a verifier can check it without asking the log.

post.summary: Trellis MCP (Streamable HTTP, stateless JSON-RPC 2.0)
post.description: One JSON-RPC 2.0 message per request: initialize, ping, tools/list and tools/call (list_models, list_attested_models, chat, verify_provider, get_receipt, verify_receipt), plus notifications, which get an empty 202. Replies are JSON, never a stream; there are no sessions. Only the chat tool needs an API key, which it spends like /api/v1/chat/completions. chat takes lane (public or attested) and disclosure (none, policy or any), meaning provider.lane and provider.disclosure: on the attested lane a prompt goes only to a provider with a fresh attestation the router verified and attested retention, and when none can answer the tool returns an error (no_attested_endpoint or disclosure_unavailable; nothing sent, nothing charged). Its result reports lane, the disclosure class the receipt records and, for an attested gateway, upstream_attestation (attested, gpu_attested, receipt_verified). list_attested_models lists the models the attested lane can serve now, with gpu_attested (true, false, or null before any verified gateway receipt). verify_provider takes provider_id and returns the router's attestation record for it in plain terms: status, TEE, verifiers, TLS pin, transparency-log status and not_checked; it is the same record as GET /api/v1/attestation/{providerId}. A connection can be made attested by default with the lane query parameter or the X-Trellis-Lane header on the /mcp URL (disclosure and X-Trellis-Disclosure-Max set a ceiling): the strictest setting wins, a call cannot relax it, and an unrecognised value refuses the chat call. Malformed JSON or a batch gets HTTP 400, a request carrying a foreign Origin header gets 403 and GET gets 405; all three carry a JSON-RPC error body.

parameters.name: lane
parameters.description: Connection default for the chat tool: public (default) or attested. attested sends every chat prompt only to attested providers and refuses the call when none can answer. Repeat or combine with the header: the strictest applies. unlinkable is not available over MCP.

parameters.name: disclosure
parameters.description: Connection default disclosure ceiling for the chat tool: none, policy or any (default). The strictest of this, the header and the call's own setting applies.

parameters.name: X-Trellis-Lane
parameters.description: Same as the lane query parameter.

parameters.name: X-Trellis-Disclosure-Max
parameters.description: Same as the disclosure query parameter.

200.description: A JSON-RPC 2.0 response: a result, or an error object with a JSON-RPC code.

202.description: Notification accepted; the body is empty.

post.summary: Save a routing policy callable as model @route/<slug>
post.description: Owner or admin. No prompt text is stored.

409.description: route_exists, route_limit_reached (100 per account), or route_lane_unavailable: the route pins the attested lane or a disclosure ceiling and a model in its list has no provider that meets it right now (metadata.unavailable_models names them; nothing is saved).

patch.summary: Update or rename a saved route
patch.description: Each config section sent replaces that section; null clears it.

409.description: route_exists, or route_lane_unavailable (see createRoute).

get.summary: List the account's presets at their latest version
Get a preset (the latest version, or ?version=)

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: A version number (3 or v3) or a hash prefix of at least 7 hex characters.

put.summary: Create a preset or save a new version
put.description: Owner or admin. The body is the whole document. A change appends an immutable version; an unchanged document adds nothing (changed: false). Models, the lane and the size caps are checked as for a saved route.

200.description: A new version, or the unchanged latest one.

409.description: preset_limit_reached (100 per account), preset_version_limit (100 versions per preset), or route_lane_unavailable (a model has no provider that meets the preset's lane or disclosure ceiling right now).

delete.summary: Delete a preset and every version of it

get.summary: List a preset's versions, newest first
JSON diff between two versions of a preset

post.description: Owner or admin. Appends a version with the content (and hash) of the one named; nothing is rewritten or deleted.

version.description: A version number or a hash prefix.

200.description: The new latest version (changed: false when it was already current).

409.description: preset_version_limit, preset_invalid, or route_lane_unavailable: the version's models can no longer be served under its lane.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Opaque cursor returned in next. Pass it through without parsing; a plain ISO-8601 timestamp is also accepted.

post.summary: Create a short-lived, budget-capped session key for an agent run
post.description: Owner or admin. The secret is returned once. A session cannot exceed its creator's budget, expiry or model allowlist.

get.summary: A session key's own remaining budget and time
Session detail with recent call metadata (never content)
Spend totals, projection, anomaly flag, series, breakdowns and key budgets
List alert rules and recent firings

post.summary: Create an alert rule (threshold, budget_pct or anomaly)
post.description: Owner or admin. Webhooks must be HTTPS to a public address and are delivered at most 3 times per firing.

409.description: too_many_rules (20 per account).

get.summary: A provider's disclosure profile and the class it is served under right now
get.description: Public. Every value is what the operator documented, with its own source and date; nothing is inferred from traffic. A provider with no recorded profile returns the conservative defaults (retention logs, jurisdiction unknown, legal hold undeclared, training use unknown, declared false). current.class is attested only when retention is declared attested and the provider's TEE attestation is fresh now; current.simulated is true when that attestation is a development report (never accepted in production).

put.summary: Replace a provider's disclosure profile (operator only)
put.description: Requires the operator token in X-Admin-Token or as a bearer token; an API key is not accepted. The profile is replaced as a whole: a claim that is left out reverts to its conservative default. A retention other than logs needs a legal_hold claim, and retention attested needs a provider with a TEE and attestation endpoint.

409.description: provider_not_attestable: retention attested was claimed for a provider with no TEE or attestation endpoint (or a development TEE in production).

put.summary: Declare a model's variant, license and weights provenance (operator only)
put.description: Requires the operator token in X-Admin-Token or as a bearer token; an API key is not accepted. The record is replaced as a whole. The model need not be listed by any provider yet: classify it first. native_low_refusal and abliterated are restricted variants and need license and base_model on record. status candidate routes the model to no provider until the record is written again as servable.

get.summary: Day-zero candidates and their latest scores (operator only)
get.description: Requires the operator token. When enabled, the router watches Hugging Face for new fine-tunes of the base models it is configured with, keeps those whose model card carries an allowed license (MIT or Apache-2.0 by default) and records why it rejected the rest. Status: discovered, rejected, evaluated, failed, approved or servable.

put.summary: Say which provider offer serves a candidate's weights (operator only)
put.description: The offer's model must declare the candidate's Hugging Face repository as its hugging_face_id, so an evaluation of one set of weights cannot approve a different model. From the moment a repository is a candidate, a model that declares it is routed to no provider until the candidate is servable.

409.description: repo_mismatch: the offer's model does not declare the candidate's repository. candidate_rejected: the candidate was rejected. invalid_state: the candidate is already approved.

post.summary: Run the probe sets against a candidate's endpoint (operator only)
post.description: Sends the endpoint 16 benign prompts that base models commonly over-refuse (fiction, security education, medical and legal information; none harmful or illegal), 12 capability prompts with exact checks (arithmetic, JSON format, instruction following) and the router's canary set. The scores are stored. The candidate passes when its refusal rate is at most DAYZERO_MAX_REFUSAL_RATE, its capability score at least DAYZERO_MIN_CAPABILITY, its canary accuracy at least DAYZERO_MIN_CANARY and the canary precision check does not contradict the declared quantization. An approved or servable candidate that fails loses its approval and stops being served.

409.description: no_endpoint: link an endpoint first. endpoint_unavailable: the linked offer or provider is not live. candidate_rejected: the candidate was rejected.

post.summary: Approve an evaluated candidate (operator only)

409.description: invalid_state: only an evaluated candidate can be approved.

post.summary: Make an approved candidate servable (operator only)
post.description: Succeeds only if the linked provider is served under attested retention with a fresh attestation and its attestation reports the in-enclave classifier as enabled: the same test routing applies to a request. Otherwise 409 not_servable says why and nothing changes. The router repeats this for approved candidates on every day-zero run.

409.description: invalid_state: only an approved candidate can be promoted. not_servable: no attested provider that reports the classifier serves it now; error.metadata.candidate is the candidate.

post.summary: Get a challenge to claim a model's creator royalty
post.description: Public and rate limited. The model must have a Hugging Face weights source on record. Commit file_content to the file named in file, on the main branch of hugging_face_id, then call the verify endpoint before expires_at. The address is the one that will receive the royalty.

hf_handle.description: Optional: refused if it is not the owner of the weights source.

409.description: not_claimable: the model has no Hugging Face weights source on record.

post.summary: Check the published challenge and record the royalty recipient
post.description: Public and rate limited. The router reads the repository's owner and the claim file through the Hugging Face API. The owner must still be the handle the challenge was issued to and the file must contain the challenge on its own line. On success the address becomes the model's royalty recipient at the router's default rate (5 percent unless configured otherwise, at most 20 percent): it is registered in the royalty contract first when one is configured, then recorded, and every later call to the model includes the royalty in its price. Verifying a verified claim returns it again.

409.description: claim_stale: the model's weights source changed since the challenge was issued.

410.description: claim_expired: the challenge is no longer valid; start a new claim.

502.description: chain_failed: the royalty contract registration failed and nothing was recorded; verify again. hf_unavailable: Hugging Face could not be read.

get.summary: Issuer keys, the token challenge and token prices
get.description: Public; 404 unless the router enables blind tokens. One 2048-bit RSA issuer key per denomination (1000, 10000 and 100000 token-units) per epoch (a week), published before the epoch starts. token_key_id is the SHA-256 of the key's RFC 9578 SubjectPublicKeyInfo (token_key, base64url), so a client can check the key against its id. A key issues only while its status is issuing; its tokens stay redeemable until redeem_until. Every token must carry challenge_digest, the SHA-256 of the published challenge. commitments are the per-epoch values a BlindIssuer contract records. Nothing in this response is signed: compare commitments with a value recorded independently (for example on chain) before trusting the keys.

post.summary: Buy blind tokens with credits
post.description: Debits the key's credits through the ledger and returns one blind signature per blinded message, in order. The client blinds the token inputs (RFC 9474) with the key named by token_key_id, and unblinds the signatures locally; the router stores counts only, never the blinded messages, the signatures or the tokens. Sending the same request again after a lost response returns the same signatures without charging again (replayed: true). Purchases count against the key's budget and are rate limited per key, capped per request (max_batch) and per account per day. A key restricted to some models cannot buy tokens. 404 unless the router enables blind tokens.

409.description: The key's epoch is not open yet (epoch_not_open), has ended (epoch_closed) or was revoked (token_key_revoked), or the same purchase is still being processed (purchase_in_progress).

get.description: Public; 404 unless the router enables Oblivious HTTP. One key configuration in application/ohttp-keys form: key identifier, KEM (DHKEM X25519 HKDF-SHA256), public key, and the KDF and AEAD pairs offered (HKDF-SHA256 with AES-128-GCM). The key changes every epoch (a day by default) and keeps opening requests for a grace period after that. This response is not signed: check it against the signed key list (GET /api/v1/ohttp/key-list) before use. Also served at /.well-known/ohttp-gateway.

503.description: The gateway has no usable key right now (ohttp_no_key). Retry after Retry-After.

post.summary: Oblivious HTTP gateway: unwrap an encapsulated request, serve it, wrap the response
post.description: Sent by a relay (or, without the privacy benefit, directly). The body is a message/ohttp-req: a binary HTTP request (RFC 9292) sealed to the gateway key. The gateway serves it on the router's own routes and answers 200 with a message/ohttp-res that carries the whole inner response, errors included, so an inner 4xx is inside the encapsulation. Reachable routes: POST chat/completions and completions (streaming only with chunked Oblivious HTTP), POST embeddings, POST blind/purchase, GET blind/keys, GET models; anything else is an inner 404 route_not_allowed. Of the request's headers only Authorization, Content-Type, Accept, X-Trellis-Lane and X-Trellis-Disclosure-Max are passed on. Responses are zero-padded to a multiple of 256 bytes. A relay identifies itself with Authorization: Bearer <key_id>:<secret>; a request without it is treated as direct and is not served the unlinkable lane. Errors before the request could be unwrapped are plain HTTP: 415, 413, 400, 422 (unknown key identifier or a request that does not decrypt, application/problem+json), 401 (a relay credential that is not recognised) and 429. Where the router enables chunked Oblivious HTTP (draft-ietf-ohai-chunked-ohttp; GET /api/v1/relays then lists gateway.chunked), the body may instead be a message/ohttp-chunked-req, answered with a message/ohttp-chunked-res (with Incremental: ?1) that is encrypted and sent chunk by chunk as the inner response is produced, so stream true works; the last chunk is sealed as the final one, so a response that ends without it was cut off and is incomplete. A chunked response that grows past the size limit ends without its final chunk. Do not retry a failed encapsulated request automatically; a repeated ciphertext is answered with an inner 409 replayed_request.

200.description: The encapsulated response: message/ohttp-res for a message/ohttp-req, message/ohttp-chunked-res for a message/ohttp-chunked-req.

413.description: The encapsulated request is larger than the gateway accepts.

415.description: The content type is not message/ohttp-req (or message/ohttp-chunked-req, where the router enables chunked Oblivious HTTP).

422.description: The key identifier is unknown, expired or revoked, the ciphersuite is not offered, or the request does not decrypt with the key it names. Fetch the key configuration again.

get.summary: Gateway key history, signed and hash-chained
get.description: Public; 404 unless the router enables Oblivious HTTP. Every gateway key with its configuration, acceptance window and status, the next epoch's key listed as upcoming before it is served, and the relay list. The document is signed with the router's receipt signing key (Ed25519 over the canonical JSON of data; keys at GET /api/v1/receipts/keys, also registered on chain), and each key's entry_hash chains to the one before it, so a client can pin log.head and notice a key that was removed or replaced. A key's private half is destroyed when its window ends (private_key_destroyed).

get.summary: Relays clients may use for the unlinkable lane
get.description: Public; 404 unless the router enables Oblivious HTTP. Each relay has its operator, its URL and a key_id (an identifier of the credential the relay presents to the gateway, published so it is on record; the router does not verify it beyond authenticating the relay). independent is false for a relay run by the gateway's own operator: the unlinkable lane is not served through it. Pick a relay whose operator is not the gateway operator.

patch.summary: Update an alert rule (kind cannot change; webhook_url null removes it)

post.summary: Create a message (Anthropic Messages API)
post.description: The Anthropic Messages API, for the Anthropic SDKs and Claude Code (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL set to the router). Also served at /api/v1/messages. The request is converted to a chat completion and sent through /api/v1/chat/completions inside the router, so the key, balance, limits, lane, signed receipt and response headers are those of a chat call. Authenticate with x-api-key or Authorization: Bearer. The model is a catalog id (GET /v1/models) or a name the operator mapped with ANTHROPIC_MODEL_MAP; an unmapped claude-* name is a 404 that says the router serves open models. Text, image (base64 and URL), tool_use and tool_result blocks, tools and tool_choice, stop_sequences, top_k (dropped for a provider that does not list it) and metadata.user_id (sent to the provider as user) are converted; max_tokens above the model's output limit, or above the room the context leaves after the prompt bound, is lowered to it, and the resulting cap is always sent to the provider. An image needs a model whose catalog entry declares a per-image token limit (input_token_limits.image in GET /api/v1/models): to a model that declares none the request is refused with a 400 (trellis.type unboundable_input) rather than guessed. The hold and the charge follow the chat route: the hold is a bound (prompt bytes plus the output cap) and the charge never exceeds it. Tools hosted by Anthropic, thinking and service_tier are accepted and not acted on (named in X-Trellis-Ignored); PDF documents, mcp_servers and container are refused with a 400. The reply's id is the receipt id, and its trellis object carries the lane, disclosure class, provider, cost, upstream_attestation where there is one, and the signed receipt. With stream true the events are message_start, ping, content_block_start, content_block_delta (text_delta, input_json_delta), content_block_stop, message_delta (billed usage and the trellis object) and message_stop, or an error event in place of the ending; a request the router refuses before any output is an HTTP error instead of a stream. stop_reason is end_turn, max_tokens, tool_use or refusal, and stop_sequence only when the provider names the stop string that ended the answer. Errors have Anthropic's shape with a trellis object carrying the router's own error type.

parameters.name: X-Trellis-Lane
parameters.description: public (default) or attested. attested sends the prompt only to a provider with a fresh TEE attestation the router verified and attested retention; when none can serve the model the call is refused with 409 (503 while they are down) and nothing is sent or charged. Same meaning as provider.lane; the stricter of the two applies. An unrecognised value is a 400.

parameters.name: X-Trellis-Disclosure-Max
parameters.description: Strictest ceiling on who may see the prompt: none, policy or any (default). Same meaning as provider.disclosure.

200.description: The message, or Anthropic server-sent events when stream is true.

Request-Id.description: An id for this request (req_...), also in the error body's request_id.

X-Trellis-Ignored.description: Present when the request asked for something that is accepted and not acted on: thinking, service_tier, or tools hosted by Anthropic (tool:<name>). A comma separated list.

schema.description: Anthropic SSE: each event has an event: line naming its type and a data: JSON object.

post.summary: Count the tokens of a message (upper bound)
post.description: The body of POST /v1/messages without max_tokens. Returns the router's own bound on the prompt, the figure a hold is priced at: the UTF-8 bytes of the text and of the indented JSON of tools and other structured fields (non-ASCII text counts the larger of its bytes and its NFKD-normalised bytes; characters are never divided by a ratio), plus fixed template allowances (64 tokens per request, 16 per message, 256 when tools are present), plus, for each image, the per-item token limit the model's catalog entry declares (input_token_limits.image in GET /api/v1/models). An image sent to a model that declares no such limit is refused with 400 (trellis.type unboundable_input). It is an upper bound, several times a tokenizer's count for English text, not a tokenizer's count; it costs nothing, and it needs a key. The model is read only for its per-item limits; a text-only body is counted the same for any model. Also served at /api/v1/messages/count_tokens.

Request-Id.description: An id for this request (req_...), also in the error body's request_id.

post.summary: Create a response (OpenAI Responses API)
post.description: The OpenAI Responses API, for the OpenAI Agents SDK, the Codex CLI and other Responses clients (POST /v1/responses is the same route). It is an adapter over POST /api/v1/chat/completions: the request is translated and sent to that route in-process with the same credentials and headers, so keys, wallet and per-call payment, blind tokens, limits, disclosure ceilings, lanes, signed receipts and error responses are the chat route's own, and the answer is returned in the Responses shape. With stream true the body is the Responses event stream, each frame an event: line and a data: line carrying type and sequence_number: response.created, response.in_progress, response.output_item.added, response.content_part.added, response.output_text.delta, response.output_text.done, response.content_part.done, response.function_call_arguments.delta, response.function_call_arguments.done, response.custom_tool_call_input.delta and .done, response.output_item.done and last response.completed (or response.incomplete when the answer was cut off by max_output_tokens). A failure after the stream has started is an error event followed by response.failed; there is no [DONE]. Stateless by design: nothing is stored, so store must be false (the default; true is refused), and previous_response_id, conversation, background, stored prompts and file or item references are refused with a 400 whose error.param names the field. Send the whole conversation in input on every request, including function_call and function_call_output items for tool round trips. GET, DELETE and cancel under /api/v1/responses/{id} answer 404. Function tools and custom (freeform) tools run. A custom tool, such as Codex's apply_patch, is offered to the model as a function with one string argument, input; its description, a line saying it takes freeform text and its grammar, if it has one, become the function's description, as guidance only: no grammar is enforced. A call to it comes back as a custom_tool_call item with the text as input (streamed as response.custom_tool_call_input.delta, then response.custom_tool_call_input.done), and a custom_tool_call_output input item is its result on the next turn. Hosted tools (web_search, file_search, code_interpreter, computer_use, image_generation, mcp) are refused with a 400 naming the tool, because Trellis hosts none; run the work in your own code and return it as a function_call_output or custom_tool_call_output. Route with provider (lane, disclosure and the router's other preferences) or the X-Trellis-Lane header; the stricter of the two applies, and a request no provider can serve under the lane is refused (409 lane_unavailable) with nothing sent and nothing charged. The response carries X-Receipt-Id, Inference-Id and X-Trellis-Lane (and X-Trellis-Policy-Hash where the serving endpoint attested one), and its metadata carries trellis_receipt_id, trellis_lane and, once known, trellis_disclosure. Other Responses options (include, truncation, service_tier, prompt_cache_key, safety_identifier, stream_options) are accepted and ignored.

200.description: A Response object, or the Responses event stream when stream is true.

X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE.description: Present when an x402 payment was settled for this call: base64 JSON {success, transaction, network, payer}.

PAYMENT-RESPONSE.description: x402 v2: the same settlement as X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE, with the same value.

schema.description: SSE frames (event: and data: lines) in the order described above; the response.completed, response.incomplete and response.failed frames carry the whole Response object.

get.summary: Not available: responses are not stored
get.description: Always 404 (responses_not_stored), like DELETE and POST .../cancel and GET .../input_items on this path. Trellis is stateless: it stores no responses, conversations or input items, so there is nothing to retrieve. A response is returned by the call that creates it. The call's signed receipt, which holds no prompt or answer, is at GET /api/v1/receipts/{id}: the id is in the X-Receipt-Id header and the response's metadata.trellis_receipt_id.

post.summary: Answer a question from documents you send, keeping nothing
post.description: Retrieval-augmented answers over documents sent with the question, with nothing kept. The router cuts the documents into overlapping chunks, embeds the chunks and the question through POST /api/v1/embeddings (in batches), ranks the chunks by cosine similarity in memory, and answers from the best top_k through POST /api/v1/chat/completions, citing numbered sources. Every call is an ordinary call of your key: billed, limited, routed by lane and receipted, and the response lists every receipt id with its lane, the disclosure class it was served under and, for an attested gateway, its upstream_attestation check. Needs a prepaid API key (Authorization: Bearer); per-call payment and blind tokens are not accepted. Lane: send provider.lane (public or attested) or provider.disclosure (none, policy, any), or the X-Trellis-Lane and X-Trellis-Disclosure-Max headers, and every call is held to exactly that and refused, never downgraded: on the attested lane 503 no_attested_endpoint (error.metadata.reason none_attested, or attested_endpoints_down with Retry-After); with only a disclosure ceiling 409 disclosure_unavailable, or 503 disclosure_provider_unavailable while qualifying providers are down; or 502 upstream_not_attested when an attested gateway's receipt does not show an attested upstream (the reply is withheld and the call is billed). A lane or ceiling pinned on the key (routing.provider) applies to every step, not only the chat call. A model the router resolves itself (a saved route, an alias of the key, trellis/...) can pin a lane of its own, so a request naming one must state provider.lane (400 lane_required). Send none and the attested lane is used when the chat model and the embedding model both have an attested endpoint; otherwise the public lane is used and lane_note says why. embedding_model defaults to qwen/qwen3-embedding-8b, else the cheapest embedding model, preferring models with an attested endpoint. Unlinkable is not available. An error from a step is that step's own status and error.type, with error.metadata.step (embeddings or chat) and error.metadata.receipts, the calls already made and billed. Caps (configurable): 200 documents, 2 MiB of document text, 2000 chunks and 64 embeddings calls per request, 413 payload_too_large above them. With stream true the embeddings run first (a refusal there, or at the start of the chat call, is an ordinary JSON error); the stream then sends a chat.completion.chunk event with choices [] and rag.object rag.sources (the sources and the embeddings receipts), the chat stream exactly as /api/v1/chat/completions sends it, an event with rag.object rag.summary (all receipts, totals and, if the chat call was refused mid-stream, error), and data: [DONE]. Nothing of the documents, the question or the answer is stored. The documents, their chunks and vectors and the question live in the memory of the one request that carries them and are dropped when it ends; this endpoint writes them to no database, cache or file, does not log them and never uses the response cache. What remains is what any call leaves: each embeddings call and the chat call is a generation of the key, with a signed receipt holding ids, model, provider, lane, token counts, cost, timing and the SHA-256 of the request and of the response, not their text (a hash confirms an exact guess; it does not reveal text). The text does leave the router: the chunks and the question go to the embedding model's provider and the question and the best chunks go to the chat model's provider. What those providers see and keep depends on the lane; on the attested lane only providers with attested retention and a fresh attestation the router verified are used, which shows what code is running, not what it does with the text.

The headers are those of the chat call, except X-Trellis-Disclosure, which is the weakest class among all the calls (and is left out when a call's class is not known), and X-Trellis-Policy-Hash, which is sent only when every call reported the same one.

post.summary: Create a batch of chat or embeddings requests, run in the background
post.description: Also at POST /v1/batches. The OpenAI Batch API shape without files: send the lines inline as requests (a list) or input_jsonl (JSON Lines text), one request per line with a unique custom_id (at most 64 characters), method POST, a url of /v1/chat/completions or /v1/embeddings (the /api/v1 forms are accepted too) and the request body. endpoint, when given, must match every line's url. input_file_id is refused with 400: there is no files endpoint, so send requests or input_jsonl. stream true, council mode (model trellis/council) and verify are refused in a batch. A batch with an invalid line is not created: the 400 invalid_request carries error.metadata.errors, a list of { line, code, message } with 1-based line numbers. Every line's prompt bound is checked before the batch is accepted: a line whose input cannot be bounded is listed with code unboundable_input (non-text input to a model that declares no input_token_limits for it, an unknown content-part type, a provider-side tool, web_search_options), and a line that batches too many prompts with code prompt_batch_too_large. Each line is held, capped and charged as a normal call is: an explicit output cap is sent to the provider and the charge never exceeds the line's hold. Needs a prepaid key. The lines run on the router's worker in spare capacity, so a batch can take minutes; lines not run within the 24h completion window expire and are not charged. Each line is billed at the normal price (BATCH_DISCOUNT_BPS is 0 by default; an operator can set a batch reduction only where a margin of at least that size funds it), a failed line is not charged, and every answered line gets its own signed receipt. Lanes, provider preferences, key budgets and key rate limits apply to each line exactly as to a normal call. Limits (operator settings): BATCH_MAX_LINES (1000 lines), BATCH_MAX_BYTES (8 MiB of input) and BATCH_MAX_ACTIVE (2 unfinished batches per key; one more is refused with 429 batch_limit); a batch over the line or byte limit is refused. The request lines and answers are never written to the database: until the results expire they are kept sealed (AES-256-GCM, with a key derived from the router's secret) in Redis, or in the router's memory without Redis, and then deleted. The database keeps only counts, costs, statuses and generation ids.

post.summary: End-to-end encrypted chat (attested gateway)
post.description: Off by default (E2EE_PASSTHROUGH_ENABLED=false). Exact JSON bytes and encrypted fields are forwarded unchanged; SSE bytes pass through unchanged. Message content is restored inside the attested gateway enclave, which forwards it to the serving workload over a separate confidential channel. Model, sizes, timing, public keys and payment metadata remain visible. Only the attested-gateway provider and text chat are supported; tools, files, search and unknown fields are refused. Holds use a conservative input-byte bound plus max_tokens. Charges trust gateway-reported usage; completion or truncation without usage charges the hold. The charge never exceeds the hold: when the gateway reports usage priced above it, the receipt carries e2ee.over_hold (USD string, the list price of the reported usage) and the gateway is paid no more than was charged. The router cannot check the restored plaintext request hash; clients must independently verify attestation and complete signed wire receipts. Prepaid keys and blind tokens are supported.

post.summary: Pay an x402 tool from the key's balance
post.description: TOOLS_MARKET_ENABLED defaults to false and is not switched on at trellis.example yet; every route answers 404 while it is off. See /docs/#paid-tools. The router fetches the resource unpaid and reads its 402 (x402 v1 JSON body with accepts, or the v2 PAYMENT-REQUIRED header). It pays only scheme exact in USDC on Solana. A quote above max_price (the seller's price plus the router's take, TOOLS_TAKE_BPS), above TOOLS_MAX_PRICE_USD or outside the key's rulebook (tools.allow, tools.deny, tools.max_price_per_call, tools.daily_budget, caps, approval) is refused before anything is held or paid. Otherwise it holds price plus take, signs a USDC transfer authorization from the router's buyer wallet to the seller's payTo and retries with X-PAYMENT or PAYMENT-SIGNATURE. A 2xx JSON or plain-text answer of at most 2 MB is charged once and returned as untrusted data with a signed tool.call receipt (COSE_Sign1; check it with POST /api/v1/receipts/verify). Any other answer is not charged: the hold is released once the authorization expires unused, or the call is charged if the seller collected it anyway. then hands the answer to a model and needs tools.pass_to_models in the rulebook.

The answer also says where what is left of this deposit returns if the key's credits are ever closed (refund_to: the token account it is paid from). Refused above the per-key cap (400 deposit_refused). 503 chain_unavailable when the Solana RPC cannot be reached. By default (`register_owner`) a key with no owner wallet gets the paying wallet registered as its owner in the same transaction; the response says so under `data.owner`.

register_owner.description: When the key has no owner wallet yet, the returned transaction also registers `payer` as the key's owner (set_key_authority, signed by the key): the transaction then carries the key's signature and the wallet adds its own with a partial sign. `false` returns the deposit alone.
