post.summary: Close the key's credits: what is left returns to the wallets that paid in
post.description: The only customer-initiated outflow (docs §5.1). A closure refund can only return to the wallets that deposited to the key: each gets at most what it put in, to the token account it named on chain (by default the one it paid from). The key can ask for a closure and take it back; it cannot choose or change a destination, so holding an API key is not enough to move a balance anywhere new. The request therefore carries only payer; one that carries refund_to is refused with 400 refund_destination_fixed. The answer lists who will be paid in refunds. Must be called with the key itself (not a sub-key; 403 forbidden otherwise). trellis_credits::close_account is authorised by the key itself: its own ed25519 keypair (the one whose public key hashes to the key hash) must sign, and no wallet can close a key, whoever deposited to it. The request carries the key, so the router signs the transaction as the key (it stores neither the key nor its keypair) and returns it in transaction with signed_by_key true. payer (any wallet) adds its signature as fee payer, pays the network fee and a small rent, and sends it before expires_at_block_height; nothing else in the transaction may change. The transaction is a single close_account instruction. Once the closure is on chain the key is frozen: anything that would spend answers 409 credits_closing until the refund is paid or the closure is cancelled (POST /api/v1/credits/close/cancel). The settlement service pays the refund after the program's delay (72 hours at launch), once no call is in progress, and a sanctions screen of the account being paid: what the key had not spent, never more than its own deposits cover. Never on demand, never sent by the router. It is not paid while the key is disabled (see POST /api/v1/credits/close/release). 201 for a new closure, 200 when one is already open (transaction null when it is already registered on chain). 400 nothing_to_close when the key has no on-chain credits or is already closed. With as_owner: true and payer = the key's registered owner wallet (see POST /api/v1/credits/owner-tx) the answer is an unsigned close_account_by_owner transaction for that wallet (signed_by_key false, requested_by owner): a closure asked for this way cannot be cancelled with the API key. The refund is split over the depositors largest remaining share first. Deposits are at least 1 USDC.

post.description: Returns a trellis_credits::cancel_close transaction already signed by the key (called with the key itself; 403 forbidden otherwise) for payer, any wallet, to sign as fee payer and send. The key itself only for a closure the key asked for, and once in 60 days: 409 cancel_cooldown (error.metadata.retry_at) after that, 403 not_requester for a closure the owner wallet asked for, 403 not_owner when as_owner is sent with another wallet. A wallet that only deposited to the key cannot cancel.

The API key has no say in it and is not part of the transaction; this route only builds it. It moves no money now. 404 not_found when that wallet has not deposited to this key.

post.summary: Get a single-use wallet sign-in challenge
post.description: No key. Returns a single-use nonce and the exact message the wallet signs: a Sign-In-With-Solana text (the EIP-4361 layout) that names this router's domain (the host of its public URL) on its first line, then the wallet's address, a statement, and URI, Version, Chain ID (the network, CAIP-2), Nonce, Issued At and Expiration Time. A wallet shows the domain, so a challenge relayed by another site is visibly not that site's: a client should check that domain is the router it is talking to and that the message names its own address before signing. Rate limited per address (429). The challenge expires after five minutes and is consumed by POST /api/v1/auth/wallet.

address.description: Base58 Solana address (32-byte ed25519 public key).

post.summary: Sign in with a wallet and get a management key
post.description: No key. The wallet signs the exact UTF-8 bytes of the message returned with the challenge (POST /api/v1/auth/wallet/challenge) with its ed25519 key (solana:signMessage) and sends the 64-byte signature base58. The router verifies the signature over the message it issued and stored with the challenge, and over nothing else: a signature over any other text does not sign in, including the earlier client-built form "trellis:wallet:v1\n<nonce>\n<timestamp>", which named no site and is retired. The router checks that the nonce exists, is unexpired, was issued for this address and this router and is used once (consumed in the same transaction that issues the key). message may be sent back; when present it must equal the issued one. Issues a management key for the wallet's account w_<address>; the secret is returned once. A wallet keeps at most ten live sign-in keys: issuing another disables the oldest. 401 invalid_wallet_auth for any failure.

timestamp.description: Sent by v1 clients. Not read: the validity is part of the signed message.

signature.description: Base58 ed25519 signature (64 bytes) over the UTF-8 bytes of the challenge's message.

message.description: Optional: the message that was signed. When sent it must be exactly the one issued with the challenge; it is never verified in its place.

get.summary: Schemes and networks this facilitator settles
get.description: Public. Each (x402Version, scheme, network) the facilitator settles, with the fee payer (relay) address and, for tab, the program id and the pre-audit cap. kinds is empty while the facilitator is switched off. No-store.

post.summary: Verify a payment without moving funds
post.description: Public. exact: decodes the transaction, checks fee payer, instructions (one TransferChecked of the USDC asset to payTo's associated token account, decimals 6), amount >= the requirement, the payer's signature and that the blockhash is still valid. tab: parses the voucher, reads the Tab account, checks payee, mint, expiry, cap, sequence and the session-key signature, and that cumulative_used covers the amount; when payload.transaction is present it must be exactly the payee-signed close for that voucher. Answers 200 with isValid false and a reason rather than an error; 400 invalid_request for a malformed body; 503 facilitator_disabled when switched off.

post.summary: Co-sign as fee payer and submit
post.description: Public. Verifies like /verify, then claims the payment by (payer, nonce) so a replay settles once and gets the same answer (409 payment_already_claimed while another settlement of the same payment is in flight; a settled replay answers the original transaction), co-signs the transaction with the relay key as fee payer and submits it, waiting for confirmation. exact: USDC moves payer to payTo. tab: the payee-signed close moves escrow to the payee and refunds the remainder to the payer; payload.transaction is required (tab_close_transaction_required). The SOL fee is recovered inside the settlement amount when a SOL price is configured (sponsorship, docs §5.2); the facilitator fee (0 during the waiver) is a second transfer. 400 with success false for a rejected payment or a failed submission (settle_transaction_failed, invalid_exact_svm_payload_transaction_blockhash_expired, invalid_tab_close_blockhash_expired).

default.description: A rejected payment or a failed submission answers 400 with this body: success false and errorReason naming why (a malformed request body is the ApiError 400 invalid_request instead).

get.description: Public, no key, no body. The latest completed hour per grade (G-S small, G-M medium, G-L large open models served on the sealed lane) and the 24-hour series. Hours are computed from paid, completed receipts with wash trading removed (self-dealing: payer and host under one account; circular: mutual payment loops; below the minimum). HVX is a public statistic; nothing settles against it. Cache-Control: public, max-age=60.

The wallet must hold a tier with a vote right now; the vote counts with that tier's fixed vote_weight, never the balance, and is checked again when the poll closes. Signed with X-Wallet-Auth for this POST (the method, the router's host and this path), where the hash is the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the body (keys sorted, no spaces). At most 10 attempts a minute per wallet. Advisory: the result does not carry anything out.

The transaction is signed here as the key; the wallet named in owner signs as the new owner and as fee payer and sends it. First registration wins, and afterwards the key alone can never change the owner (only the owner wallet can, on chain). The owner can close the key without the key (POST /api/v1/credits/close with as_owner) and take back any closure; it gains no claim on the balance, which still only returns to the wallets that deposited. Do this when the key is created, before it can leak. 400 no_credit_account before the first deposit, 409 owner_already_registered (error.metadata.owner), 409 credits_closing.

BearerAuth.description: Send the key in Authorization. Never put it in a URL.

AnthropicApiKey.description: Anthropic SDK style: the Trellis key in x-api-key. Authorization: Bearer with the same key works too. Never put it in a URL.

WalletAuth.name: X-Wallet-Auth
WalletAuth.description:
X-Wallet-Auth: <base58 address>:<unixSeconds>:<base58 ed25519 signature>, where the signature, by the wallet whose public key is the address, is over the UTF-8 bytes of trellis:wallet-auth:v2
<METHOD>
<host>
<path>
<unixSeconds>
<sha256 hex> (six lines joined by line feeds, no trailing one): METHOD is the request method in upper case; host is the router's public host as configured, with its port if it has one, in lower case (the value the sign-in challenge calls domain); path is the request path with its query string, as sent; the last line is the SHA-256 of what the route binds. What a route binds: the chat routes bind the canonical JSON (keys sorted, no whitespace) of the body without stream and stream_options; other JSON routes bind the canonical JSON of the body; a GET binds the empty string; GET /api/v1/hosts/{providerId} binds the string "GET /api/v1/hosts/<url-encoded providerId>". Valid for five minutes and single use per (address, timestamp, method, host, path, hash): a signature for one route, method or router is refused on any other. The earlier message, trellis:<unixSeconds>:<sha256>, named no method, path or host and is no longer accepted (401 invalid_wallet_auth; error.metadata carries version and host). Lets a wallet spend the change left on its account w_<address> by earlier x402 payments, binds a bare transaction signature in X-PAYMENT to the wallet that paid, lets a host operator read its private host fields and sign up a host, and signs a holder's advisory vote. Never authorizes a payment by itself.

PrivateToken.name: Authorization
PrivateToken.description: Only where the router enables blind tokens. `PrivateToken token=<base64url>`: one Privacy Pass token (RFC 9578 type 0x0002, 354 bytes) bought with POST /api/v1/blind/purchase. Each token can be spent once.

Payment.name: X-Payment
Payment.description: Payment for this exact request, where the router has x402 enabled (data.per_call.x402 in GET /api/v1/status): either base64 JSON {x402Version: 1, scheme: "exact", network, payload: {transaction}} for the requirement in the 402 body, where transaction is a base64 Solana transaction that holds exactly one SPL TransferChecked of USDC (EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v, 6 decimals) from the payer's token account to payTo's associated token account, with extra.feePayer as fee payer (its signature slot left empty) and the payer's signature present, no address lookup tables; or the base58 signature of such a transfer already sent and finalized. The fee payer co-signs only inside fixed bounds and refuses anything else before it signs: exactly two required signatures (the fee payer and the payer); the fee payer named by no instruction; at most one SetComputeUnitLimit (at most 200,000 units) and one SetComputeUnitPrice (at most 5,000,000 micro-lamports per unit) with a priority fee, ceil(limit x price / 1e6), of at most 10,000 lamports (with no explicit limit the fee is computed on 200,000 units per other instruction); at most one idempotent creation of payTo's associated token account, funded by the payer and never by the fee payer; no other program. A bare transaction signature is accepted only together with X-Wallet-Auth from the wallet that paid, signed for this request: a landed payment is public, so the signature alone does not show who is asking (401 payment_not_bound_to_caller without it, 402 with the same type when another wallet signed). The facilitator co-signs as fee payer, submits, and serves the call; unused value stays as change on the account w_<payer>. Rejections are a fresh 402 with payment_error (for example invalid_exact_svm_payload_transaction_amount_mismatch, invalid_exact_svm_payload_transaction_blockhash_expired, invalid_exact_svm_payload_transaction_instructions_compute_price_instruction_too_high, invalid_exact_svm_payload_transaction_create_ata_instruction, invalid_exact_svm_payload_transaction_fee_payer_included_in_instruction_accounts, payment_already_claimed). Do not replay blindly.

PaymentSignature.name: PAYMENT-SIGNATURE
PaymentSignature.description: x402 v2 form of X-PAYMENT: base64 JSON PaymentPayload {x402Version: 2, resource, accepted, payload: {transaction}} for the requirement in PAYMENT-REQUIRED, with the same base64 Solana transaction. Read like X-PAYMENT; do not replay blindly.

PaymentRecovery.name: PAYMENT-RECOVERY
PaymentRecovery.description: x402 payment recovery, where data.per_call.x402.recovery.available is true: the payer's base58 ed25519 signature of the UTF-8 text trellis:x402-recovery:<network>:<payer>:<nonce> (data.per_call.x402.recovery.message gives the template; nonce is the payer's transaction signature). Sent with the same X-PAYMENT or PAYMENT-SIGNATURE and the identical request after a paid answer was lost, it returns the answer kept for that payer and nonce byte for byte, with the same settlement headers, and never relays the payment again. Kept 24 hours. Refusals: 401 invalid_payment_recovery, 409 payment_request_mismatch, 404 payment_recovery_not_found with metadata.settled.

PayWith.name: X-Pay-With
PayWith.description: Pay with a tokenized stock (docs §6): the base58 mint of an xStock or other tokenized stock with a Jupiter route. A Swig session key with a per-day cap in that token signs an ExactOut swap for the USDC owed, batched until 1 USD or 24 hours; the fill must be within 1% of the oracle value, and a mint whose Scaled UI Amount multiplier changes within 24 hours falls back to credits. On any failure the call is paid from prepaid credits, then 402. Only for keys with a pay-with session; a key's pay_with_default applies when the header is absent.

DisclosureMax.name: X-Trellis-Disclosure-Max
DisclosureMax.description: Same as provider.disclosure. When both are given the stricter one applies.

Lane.name: X-Trellis-Lane
Lane.description: Same as provider.lane. When both are given the stricter one applies. unlinkable is served only where the router enables Oblivious HTTP or serves the lane over its Tor onion service (otherwise 501), and then only through a relay, or through the onion service, with a blind token.

LaneDowngrade.name: X-Trellis-Lane-Downgrade
LaneDowngrade.description: Same as provider.lane_downgrade: attested lets a request for lane unlinkable that carries an API key or a wallet be served on lane attested. none in either setting refuses the downgrade.

TlogSha256.name: sha256
TlogSha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the key or configuration.

DecisionTag.name: X-Trellis-Decision-Tag
DecisionTag.description: Optional sha256:<64 hex>, for example the SHA-256 of the order intent this call informs. Signed into the receipt as payload.decision_tag and v2 claims.decision_tag. Refused with 400 invalid_decision_tag when malformed and 400 decision_tag_unlinkable on the unlinkable lane. Ignored while DECISION_TAGS_ENABLED is false (the default).

TrellisTab.name: X-Trellis-Tab
TrellisTab.description: The tab x402 scheme (docs §5.2, program trellis_tab): the base58 address of an open Tab account whose payee is this router (opened by the payer's wallet with open_tab(payer, payee, mint = USDC, cap, expiry, session_key), which moves cap into the tab's escrow; expiry is at most 30 days out; a tab bound to the payer's rulebook also passes the rulebook, the rules config and the rules program to open_tab and top_up, never to close or reclaim). Sent together with X-Trellis-Tab-Voucher on every request the tab pays for; the router bills the voucher delta and stops serving when unvouched usage exceeds max(0.25 x last request cost, 0.05 USDC). On close the payee posts the highest voucher: the program pays cumulative_used and refunds the rest; anyone can reclaim 24 hours after expiry if no close happened (no signature is needed: the payee gets its highest posted voucher, the payer the rest).

TrellisTabVoucher.name: X-Trellis-Tab-Voucher
TrellisTabVoucher.description: The voucher for X-Trellis-Tab: base64 of the 110-byte message "trellis:tab:voucher:v1" (22 ASCII bytes) || the tab program id (32 bytes) || tab (32 bytes) || Tab.created_at i64 little-endian || cumulative_used u64 little-endian || seq u64 little-endian, a dot, then base64 of the 64-byte ed25519 signature of that message by the tab's session key (registered at open_tab; the wallet itself never signs vouchers). The domain string keeps a voucher from being any other message the key signed; the program id binds it to one deployment, and so to one cluster; created_at (the time the program recorded when open_tab landed, read from the Tab account) binds it to one opening of the tab address, so a voucher of a closed tab is worth nothing against a tab opened again at the same address. Only this form is accepted: the earlier 48-byte message (tab || cumulative_used || seq) is refused (400 invalid_tab_voucher). cumulative_used is the total in USDC base units the payer authorizes so far and must not decrease; seq must strictly increase per tab; cumulative_used may not exceed the tab's cap. Refusals: 402 voucher_required (unvouched usage over the allowance), 402 cap_exceeded, 402 voucher_wrong_program (signed for another tab program), 402 voucher_wrong_tab_opening (signed for an earlier opening of this tab address), 402 invalid_voucher_signature, 402 voucher_stale, 402 tab_not_found, 402 tab_expired.

RouteExplanation.description: V84: compact JSON RouteExplanation, on chat/text completions and embeddings when ROUTE_EXPLAIN_ENABLED is true (default false; switched on at trellis.example). The signed receipt route claim has the same fields. Streams wait for the serving provider before sending this header and also deliver the claim in the final receipt. Cache and encrypted-chat paths omit it.

Disclosure.description: The disclosure class the answering provider was served under: attested (retention declared attested and a fresh TEE attestation), policy (a documented no-retention policy, no legal hold) or vendor-forwarded (anything else). On a stream it is sent only when every provider the request can reach shares one class; the signed receipt always carries it.

LaneServed.description: The lane the request was served under: public (any provider), attested (only providers under attested retention with a fresh attestation) or unlinkable (attested providers, reached through an Oblivious HTTP relay or over Tor through the router's onion service, and paid with a blind token). It is the lane the router enforced: the one the request asked for (or its key's or saved route's default), attested when an unlinkable request with a key allowed that downgrade, unlinkable for a relayed blind-token request that named none, and otherwise public.

ReceiptId.description: The id of this generation's signed receipt: the same value as the response's id and receipt.id. Read the receipt with GET /api/v1/receipts/{id}. On a stream it is sent before the first chunk; the final event carries the receipt itself.

InferenceId.description: The same id as X-Receipt-Id, under the header name Hugging Face inference clients read.

PolicyHash.description: Present only when the serving endpoint's fresh, verified attestation bound the hash of the policy its in-enclave classifier enforces ("sha256:<64 hex>"). Omitted otherwise, and on a stream unless every endpoint the request can reach attested the same hash. The router relays the attested value; it never computes one.

ApiError.description: OpenRouter-shaped API error. A 402 payment response may include payment metadata and is not a signal to repeat payment automatically.

BadRequest.description: The request body, JSON or parameters failed validation. error.type is, for example, invalid_request, invalid_json or invalid_guardrails; do not retry the same request unchanged. On chat, completions, embeddings and the Messages, Responses and Ollama adapters it can also be unboundable_input: the request carries input whose token count has no upper bound, so no hold can be priced for it (image, audio, video or file input to a model whose catalog entry declares no input_token_limits for that kind, with error.metadata.kinds; an unknown content-part type, with error.metadata.part_type; a provider-side tool, which is a tools entry whose type is not function; web_search_options; or an embeddings input that is neither text nor token ids). Send text, or choose a model that declares the limit. On /completions, prompt may be a string, an array of strings, an array of token ids or an array of token-id arrays, and each string or id array of a list is its own completion, held and priced as one: more than 16 (operator setting HOLD_MAX_PROMPT_BATCH; error.metadata.max) is prompt_batch_too_large, and any other shape is invalid_request.

Unauthorized.description: Authentication is missing or was rejected: no API key, an unknown, disabled or expired key, or invalid wallet authentication. error.type is missing_key, invalid_key, key_disabled, key_expired or invalid_wallet_auth.

PaymentRequired.description: The call cannot be paid: the balance or the key's budget is insufficient (insufficient_credits, key_budget_exceeded; the balance must cover the hold, error.metadata.required_usd, which is the request's worst case and a bound, not an estimate: the prompt's bytes plus the output cap, so a lower max_tokens lowers it, and what the call does not use is released when it settles),a per-call payment is required or was not accepted (payment_required with the x402 requirement in the body and payment_error naming the reason, payment_pending while a bare transaction signature is not finalized, payment_failed, per_call_too_large above the per-call maximum), or a tab voucher is needed (voucher_required, cap_exceeded, tab_expired). A payment_required body is also the x402 v1 PaymentRequirementsResponse {x402Version: 1, error, accepts: [X402Requirement], price_usdc, model} and binds to this exact request; never repeat a payment automatically.

PAYMENT-REQUIRED.description: Present when the router has x402 enabled: the x402 v2 PaymentRequired (base64 JSON {x402Version: 2, error, resource: {url, description, mimeType}, accepts: [{scheme: "exact", network, amount, asset, payTo, maxTimeoutSeconds, extra: {feePayer, decimals}}]}) for the same price as the body, with the CAIP-2 network (mainnet solana:5eykt4UsFv8P8NJdTREpY1vzqKqZKvdp) and amount in USDC base units.

PAYMENT-RESPONSE.description: x402 v2, only when a payment was rejected or its settlement failed: base64 JSON {success: false, errorReason, transaction: "", network, payer}.

Forbidden.description: The key is valid but may not do this: its role does not allow the action, or its model allowlist excludes the model. error.type is forbidden or model_not_allowed. On a model call it can also be early_access: the model is inside its early-access window and not open to the caller yet. error.metadata then holds model, opens_at, early_access_until and tier (the caller's tier name or null), Retry-After gives the seconds until it opens to the caller, and nothing is charged. On a holder vote it is not_a_holder: the wallet holds no tier with a vote.

Retry-After.description: With early_access: seconds until the model opens to the caller.

NotFound.description: The model, provider route, key, team, generation or receipt does not exist or is not visible to the caller. error.type is, for example, not_found, model_not_found or no_providers.

DisclosureUnavailable.description: 409 disclosure_unavailable. No provider meets provider.disclosure, though the model has providers that would otherwise serve the request (a lane that no attested endpoint can serve is 503 no_attested_endpoint instead). On chat completions it can also be verification_unavailable: verify "dual" found fewer than two providers of the model that support temperature and seed (on lane attested: fewer than two different attested providers of the model). The request is never routed to a provider that does not meet the setting; nothing was sent to any provider and nothing was charged. Also credits_closing: the key's credits are being closed (the closure from POST /api/v1/credits/close is registered on chain), so the key is frozen until its refund is paid; error.metadata.closure names the closure, and retrying with the same key does not help.

LaneNotAvailable.description: 501 lane_not_available. Lane unlinkable is not available on this router: it needs the Oblivious HTTP gateway, or the lane over its Tor onion service, with blind tokens, which it does not run. Nothing was sent to any provider.

DisclosureProviderDown.description: 503. no_attested_endpoint: lane attested or unlinkable, and no endpoint of the model with a fresh, verified attestation can serve it; error.metadata.reason is none_attested, or attested_endpoints_down (with Retry-After) when attested endpoints exist but are all in an outage. A council with an attested seat (a member or the judge) that has none is refused the same way, and error.metadata.council_seat names the seat. disclosure_provider_unavailable: providers that meet provider.disclosure exist but are all in an outage right now; retry after Retry-After. Either way the request is not routed to any other provider and nothing was charged.

TooManyRequests.description: A rate limit was reached (rate_limited). Wait for the Retry-After interval before retrying.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying, when the limit reports it.

AnthropicError.description: Anthropic's error shape, for the Messages endpoints. error.type follows the status: 400 invalid_request_error, 401 authentication_error, 402 billing_error, 403 permission_error, 404 not_found_error, 413 request_too_large, 429 rate_limit_error (with Retry-After), 5xx api_error, 504 timeout_error. A status Anthropic does not define keeps its own (409 for a lane no provider can serve, 501 for a lane the router does not run) and sends X-Should-Retry: false. trellis carries the router's own error type and metadata, and the receipt_id when a refused call was billed. A 400 whose trellis.type is unboundable_input is input no hold can be priced for: for example an image sent to a model whose catalog entry declares no per-image token limit (input_token_limits).

Request-Id.description: An id for this request (req_...), also in the error body's request_id.

OllamaError.description: Ollama's error shape, {"error": "..."}, with the router's status: 400 for a bad field (the message names it), 401 or 402 without a usable key, 404 for an unknown model (the message names one to use), 409 or 503 when the requested lane cannot be served, 429 with Retry-After, 501 for local-model operations, 502 when every provider failed before any output.

CreditsClosing.description: credits_closing: this key's credits are being closed. Once the closure (POST /api/v1/credits/close) is registered on chain the key is frozen and anything that would spend is refused until the refund is paid or the closure is cancelled (POST /api/v1/credits/close/cancel); error.metadata.closure is the closure's id. Not a transient error: do not retry with the same key.

error.message: This key's credits are being closed and refunded; it cannot start new calls.

NotEnabled.description: This route is not on the router's launch surface. A router running LAUNCH_SURFACE=core (the default) registers only the operations marked `x-launch-surface: core`; every other path answers this, whatever the feature's own setting says. `GET /api/v1/status` reports the surface under `data.launch_surface`.

error.message: POST /api/v1/batches is not enabled on this router (launch surface: core). GET /api/v1/status lists what is.

asked.description: Sent to ask me first; counted as not run.

stopped_at.description: Present when the draft would have stopped the key; every later call is refused.

actual.description: What happened to the same calls and actions. not_recorded counts calls that ran with no rulebook decision.

changed.description: Calls and actions whose replayed decision differs from the recorded one.

transaction.description: exact: the payer-signed base64 transaction (see X402PaymentPayload).

tab, required for /settle: the payee-signed close transaction [Ed25519(voucher), trellis_tab::close(cumulative_used, seq)] with the facilitator's relay key as fee payer, base64. The facilitator checks it is exactly that close, co-signs as fee payer and submits: escrow pays cumulative_used to the payee and refunds the rest to the payer.

FacilitatorPaymentRequest.description: The x402 facilitator request (Coinbase facilitator shape). exact: the payer's signed USDC transfer, co-signed by the relay as fee payer. tab: the voucher, plus for settlement the payee-signed trellis_tab::close the relay co-signs; the relay key only ever pays fees.

invalidReason.description: exact: invalid_exact_svm_payload_transaction*, invalid_network, unsupported_scheme, unsupported_asset, amount_below_minimum; tab: invalid_tab_voucher, tab_not_found, tab_payee_mismatch, tab_asset_mismatch, tab_expired, voucher_exceeds_cap, voucher_stale, invalid_voucher_signature, voucher_below_amount, invalid_tab_close_*, tab_close_transaction_required.

payer.description: The payer's base58 address when it could be read.

transaction.description: The base58 Solana transaction signature; empty when nothing was settled.

feePayer.description: The relay key that co-signs as fee payer.

maxCapUnits.description: tab: the largest cap a tab may hold while the programs are pre-audit.

intent.description: Routing identifiers, output limit and estimated cost only. Multi-model requests contain an intents array. No prompt or response fields.

AgentBreakers.description: Optional rolling recorded-state circuit breakers. Inclusive thresholds trip the router kill switch before the next admission with reason breaker:<field> and HTTP 403 agent_killed; no charge for the refused request. Account locking serializes observations, including inherited session admissions. Manual principal resume resets breaker observations and spend window, not cap spend. Recorded spend includes open usage reservations; in-flight work may finish. Only requests through Trellis. AGENT_POLICY_ENABLED defaults false.

alerts.description: Optional opt-in. Omission preserves behavior and hashes; empty object uses defaults. Reuses linked channels; email has no destination.

above_calls_per_hour.description: Optional. Ask the principal first once the rolling hour already holds this many model calls the rulebook admitted, plus approvals used (reason approval_calls_per_hour).

rungs.description: Requirements cannot decrease; spending multipliers must strictly increase above 1. Both thresholds apply at each rung.

team_id.description: The owning team, or null for an account-wide playbook.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the canonical rules; each following key's rulebook carries the same digest.

version.description: 1 at creation, plus one for each change of rules. A rename keeps it.

updated_by.description: Hash of the key that made the last change.

followers.description: Every key that follows the playbook.

keys.description: The following keys the caller manages.

team_id.description: Management keys only: a team the account owns.

stopped_until.description: B117: Present only on a timed stop; omitted on running or indefinitely stopped policies.

playbook_id.description: Present only while the key follows a playbook (POST /api/v1/agents/{key_hash}/playbook); its rules are then that playbook's current rules.

admission.description: Null for curated providers. Approval requires admitted probation/live status, no refusal reasons and a fresh successful latest hardware attestation plus the recorded checked policy.

policy_version.description: Version recorded by admission or renewal, not necessarily the latest published policy.

admission.description: Null for curated providers. Approval requires admitted probation/live status, no refusal reasons and a fresh successful latest hardware attestation plus the recorded checked policy.

policy_version.description: Version recorded by admission or renewal, not necessarily the latest published policy.

attestation_history.description: First 50 sanitized events from the existing attestation history endpoint, with data, next cursor, history_days and url. Null when history is disabled.

measurement.description: Existing attestation endpoint current measurement: digests, status, timestamps, hardware registers, registry state and transparency_log with Rekor entry_url and verification checks; no raw quote.

items.description: Existing attestation endpoint superseded measurements, each with its own superseded_at and transparency_log entry_url.

proof_time.description: Existing proof-time summary metadata (generated_at, history_days, fresh_within_ms) and its host record. Host is null when absent from that summary. Proof-time itself is null when history is disabled.

operator.description: Present only after walletAuth recovers the stored provider operator. Lifetime invoice units include paid invoices; unpaid units have no recorded payment transaction and can include a pending payout.

suggested_models.description: B121: optional availability-error alternatives; empty if none match. Never switches models or charges. Messages also returns this top-level field; Responses stream errors carry it in the error event and response.error.

ApiError.description: A 402 payment_required body additionally carries the x402 fields of X402PaymentRequired (x402Version, accepts, price_usdc, network_fee_max_usdc, model, payment_error). price_usdc (equal to accepts[0].maxAmountRequired in base units) is what the payment must carry: the request's worst-case price plus network_fee_max_usdc, and never less than the minimum payment (0.03 USDC by default). network_fee_max_usdc is the most the Solana network fee of an exact payment can be (0.005 USDC at the default settings); the router pays that fee and passes it on at cost, with no margin: what is kept back is the fee of the transaction as signed (5,000 lamports per signature plus its priority fee) at the router's stated SOL price, shown on the receipt as its own line (network_fee: lamports, usdc, sol_usdc, basis pass_through). Everything else is credited, and what the call does not use stays on the payer's wallet account as change. Sponsored payments are limited per payer, per source and in total, over any minute and any 24 hours (429 rate_limited); a payer whose sponsored payment failed after it was sent is refused with 403 payer_not_sponsored and can still pay its own fee and present the signature with X-Wallet-Auth. GET /api/v1/status reports lamports paid and USDC recovered under per_call.x402.network_fees.

Model.description: When UPSTREAM_MONITOR_ENABLED is on, availability is temporarily_unavailable if every eligible provider account has a last successful USD balance at or below UPSTREAM_BALANCE_EXHAUSTED_USD (default 0). This optional field is omitted otherwise. A failed check retains an exhausted state until a later reading exceeds the threshold. Account balances remain operator-only.

availability.description: Optional; all eligible upstream accounts are exhausted. Omitted otherwise.

capabilities.description: Shared catalogue tags; longContext means at least 128,000 tokens. network requires a live fresh-attested network-host offer for an admitted model. encrypted requires the separate enabled gateway path, exact model ID and fresh evidence; ordinary chat remains readable by the router.

provider_names.description: Names of providers with live servable offers for this model.

pricing.description: Prices are returned as decimal strings per token; consult the live response.

input_token_limits.description: The most prompt tokens one non-text input item can cost, per kind, as the model's providers declare it in their /models entry (the largest across them). Present only for models that declare it. A hold counts each such item at this figure; a request with image, audio, video or file input to a model that declares no figure for that kind is refused with 400 unboundable_input.

lanes.description: The lanes this model can be served on right now: public whenever it has a live endpoint; attested while one of its endpoints has attested retention and a fresh, verified attestation; unlinkable as well where the router serves that lane (Oblivious HTTP, or its Tor onion service). The endpoints listing carries the same field per endpoint.

disclosure.description: How many live endpoints are served under each disclosure class right now.

creator.description: Address that receives the model's creator royalty, once claimed.

royalty_bps.description: Creator royalty in basis points of the notional price; 0 until a creator is recorded.

variant.description: native_low_refusal and abliterated are restricted: they are routed only to providers served under attested retention with a fresh attestation whose attestation reported the in-enclave hard-block classifier as enabled. Whatever lane or disclosure setting a request carries, and however the provider is pinned, they are never sent to a public or vendor-forwarded provider.

variant_source.description: declared: an operator recorded the variant. candidate: the model is the weights of a day-zero candidate. inferred: nobody has classified the model and its name says its refusals were removed, so it is treated as abliterated. default: no record, treated as mainstream.

license.description: License identifier from the weights' model card, when an operator recorded one.

base_model.description: The model these weights derive from.

weights.description: Where the weights came from, as recorded by the operator.

revision.description: Commit the weights were taken from.

digest.description: sha256:<hex> of the weights, when recorded (for a day-zero model, the model digest in the provider's verified attestation).

creator_handle.description: Hugging Face handle of the uploader.

datacenter_region.description: The one datacenter region every live endpoint of the model reports; null when any endpoint does not report one or they differ.

routing_variants.description: Model suffixes that change how this model is routed right now: nitro (fastest providers first, as provider.sort throughput) and floor (cheapest first, as provider.sort price) always; free while a free endpoint serves it; private while an endpoint has a fresh TEE attestation.

ModelAttestation.description: What the strongest live endpoint serving the model has proven. Every value comes from the router's own attestation and measurement records; a value that is not known is null, never filled in. null when no endpoint serves the model.

best.description: The strongest disclosure class any live endpoint is served under right now (the same value as disclosure.best).

manifest_ref.description: Where that endpoint's measured image is recorded, while its attestation is fresh. null when neither is known.

rekor_entry.description: The transparency log entry uuid, once its inclusion proof was checked.

registry_tx.description: The on-chain MeasurementRegistry transaction, once the registry reports the measurement.

exec_profile_id.description: The attested execution profile. null until an attestation the router checks reports one.

policy_hash.description: The classifier policy hash that endpoint's fresh attestation bound (as sent in X-Trellis-Policy-Hash), else null.

json_check.description: V83: Requires STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_CHECK_ENABLED (default false; switched on at trellis.example). validate checks the final JSON; repair permits one correction by the same routed model/provider. Both calls are billed normally. Streaming repair validates only. Requires json_object or json_schema and n=1; no council or dual verification. Non-streaming repair requires a bearer API key and bypasses the response cache. Explicit request settings override preset defaults.

path.description: JSON Pointer path; empty string is the root.

StructuredOutputResult.description: V83: Unsigned response metadata; not written to generation receipts or returned by receipt lookup. Existing batch outputs may retain it with the answer. Original signed payload/sig/v2 stay intact. Top-level usage is for the returned call only; total_cost includes both served calls even if the correction is invalid. Checks do not establish factual accuracy. Supported schema assertions: type (including arrays), nullable, properties, required, additionalProperties, items, enum, const, anyOf, minLength/maxLength, minimum/maximum/exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum, minItems/maxItems, minProperties/maxProperties, and existing local #/ references via $defs/definitions. Unknown assertions are refused before billing. Limits: 1 MiB answer, 4096 schema nodes, 100000 validation steps, 64 levels, 16 reported errors. Oversized/non-text answers cannot be repaired.

retry_error.description: Correction did not return a usable answer. The first charge remains, and a signed correction charge is included even if its attestation was refused after settlement. status when known, reason.

repair_supported.description: false for streaming repair; no second call is made.

cost.description: Exact USDC charge for this call.

total_cost.description: Sum of the served calls' USDC charges.

model.description: Public model ID, optionally with routing suffixes: :nitro sorts providers by throughput (fastest first) and :floor by price (cheapest first), the same as provider.sort throughput and price and winning over it; both only order the providers the other preferences and the lane allow. :free and :private also apply. The reserved ID trellis/council selects council mode when the router enables it. @route/<slug> calls a saved route and @preset/<name> (or @preset/<name>@<version> to pin one version) calls a preset of the key's account. @character/<id> calls a character: the card is the prompt and models[0], or the character's default model, answers.

max_tokens.description: The output cap. Optional: the router always sends a cap to the provider, the smallest of this value, the catalog's output limit for the model (16,384 when the catalog has none) and the room the context leaves after the prompt bound. A higher value is clamped, not refused; an omitted value is filled in. The cap is what the hold prices, so a lower value lowers the hold.

max_completion_tokens.description: Same as max_tokens; the smaller of the two applies when both are sent. Sent to the provider, set to the cap, when the caller sent it.

tools.description: Requires a model/provider that supports tools.

response_format.description: Requires a model/provider that supports the requested response format.

verify.description: Send the same request to two providers of the model at temperature 0 with a fixed seed and compare the outputs. Both calls are billed. Needs the router's council feature; not combinable with stream, models, cache or n above 1. Provider preferences, disclosure ceiling and lane apply to both calls. With lane attested the two calls go to two different attested providers of the model (retention declared attested, attestation fresh); each receipt then records its provider's attestation as payload.attestation_ref, and the verification field carries attested and attestation_refs next to agree. If two such providers do not exist the answer is 409, and nothing is sent or charged.

CouncilRequest.description: Used with model trellis/council. Members are called in parallel through the normal routing path, then the judge chooses one answer (judge) or writes a final one (fuse). Every call is billed and receipted; the worst case of all calls is held up front. provider preferences, including a disclosure ceiling or lane, apply to every member and to the judge.

models.description: Member model IDs. Falls back to the router's configured default when omitted.

judge.description: Model ID of the judge. Falls back to the router's configured default when omitted.

mode.description: judge returns one member's answer unchanged; fuse returns the judge's own text and does not support tools or response_format.

max_cost_usd.description: Refuse the request with 402 council_budget_exceeded unless the worst case of every call fits. Lower max_tokens to fit.

min_members.description: Members that must answer before the judge runs. Defaults to 2.

attested.description: true holds every member and the judge to the attested lane (retention declared attested and a fresh attestation the router verified), the same as provider.lane attested for the whole council. Nothing is downgraded or dropped: a member, or the judge, with no attested provider refuses the request with 503 no_attested_endpoint, and nothing is sent or charged. The response then carries attested and attestation_refs in council, and each call's receipt carries attestation_ref. A production router has few attested providers today, so this often returns that 503.

CouncilResult.description: Present on council responses. The top-level receipt is the judge's call and its signed payload carries the same members list; its disclosure is the weakest class among all the calls.

disclosure.description: The class this member was served under.

receipt_id.description: Null for a member that failed; it was not billed.

total_cost.description: USD charged across every member and the judge.

attested.description: Present when the council ran on the attested lane (council.attested true, or lane attested). True only when every member and the judge were served under the attested class and each has a reference in attestation_refs. Signed in the top-level receipt.

attestation_simulated.description: True when any attestation behind the council is a development report; a production router never accepts one.

attestation_refs.description: One entry per call that took part, members in order and then the judge: what the router itself verified about the provider that served it. Signed in the top-level receipt.

label.description: The member's label; absent for the judge.

AttestationRef.description: The attestation the router had verified for a provider when it served a call: the hash of the attestation report and, when the provider attested through a self-signed TLS certificate, the pinned key the router's connection to it accepts. Recorded in the signed receipt of a call made under an attested council or attested dual verification, as payload.attestation_ref. Receipts made any other way do not carry it. The same data is at GET /api/v1/attestation/{providerId}.

tee.description: tdx, snp, nvidia-cc, tinfoil or dev.

report_hash.description: Hash of the attestation report the router verified (the payload.attestation field of the same receipt).

tls_pin.description: Null when the provider did not attest through a self-signed certificate.

spki_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the pinned certificate's SubjectPublicKeyInfo.

attestation_ref.description: SHA-256 of the quote the certificate names.

simulated.description: true when the report is development evidence.

VerificationResult.description: Present on verify "dual" responses. agree is true when both providers returned the same output (exactly, or after whitespace is collapsed); it says nothing about whether either provider is attested, unless the request used lane attested (then attested and attestation_refs say so). The response body is the first provider's output.

attested.description: Present only on lane attested. True when both calls were served by two different providers under the attested class and each has a reference in attestation_refs. Signed in both receipts, next to agree.

attestation_refs.description: One entry per call that ran (label A or B), in the same order as receipts. Each receipt also carries its own provider's reference as payload.attestation_ref.

ProviderPreferences.description: Provider routing preferences (order, only, ignore, sort, max_price, private and others) plus the disclosure options below.

disclosure.description: Ceiling on how a prompt may be handled. none: only providers whose retention is declared attested and whose TEE attestation is fresh. policy: those, plus providers with a documented no-retention policy and no legal hold. any: no filter. Never silently relaxed: if nothing qualifies the request fails (409, or 503 when qualifying providers are down). A request with a ceiling never uses the response cache.

lane.description: public: any endpoint; attested endpoints get attested_bonus (default 1.25) in the selection weight. attested: only endpoints with attested retention and a fresh, verified attestation, with no fallback to any other (503 no_attested_endpoint). unlinkable: the same endpoints, and only for a request that arrived through the Oblivious HTTP gateway by way of an independent relay (see Oblivious HTTP), or through the router's Tor onion service where it serves the lane that way, and is paid with a blind token; 501 where the router serves the lane on neither path, 403 lane_requires_anonymous_auth for an API key or a wallet, 403 unlinkable_requires_relay or unlinkable_requires_independent_relay, 401 unlinkable_requires_token otherwise. Unset: the key's default (routing.provider.lane), then the saved route's, then public; a request through an independent relay paid with a blind token defaults to unlinkable. provider.order, only and ignore still apply inside a lane. On attested and unlinkable the router still terminates TLS and sees the prompt; end-to-end encryption through the router is planned.

lane_downgrade.description: attested: a request for lane unlinkable that carries an API key or a wallet is served on lane attested instead of being refused with lane_requires_anonymous_auth. Never downgrades to public. Same as the X-Trellis-Lane-Downgrade header; none in either refuses the downgrade.

source.description: The document or statement the value comes from.

as_of.description: The date the source was checked.

declared.description: False when the operator has recorded nothing; every value is then the conservative default.

retention.description: attested: the provider states prompts are not retained and runs in a TEE. policy: a documented no-retention policy. logs: prompts may be logged (default).

jurisdiction.description: Where the operator is subject to legal process; unknown by default.

active.description: null = not declared. A no-retention policy is not trusted while a hold is active or undeclared.

claims.description: The source and date behind each value; null when the value is a default.

simulated.description: True when the attestation behind an attested class is a development report.

DisclosureInput.description: Every claim is optional and carries its own source and date.

management.description: Only honored for authorized authenticated sub-key creation; root-key management is never granted by this field.

tracing.description: Trace export for this key's public-lane calls; null removes it.

role.description: The new key's role in its team (default member). A key cannot hand out a role above its own. In a team with an org budget every key needs a limit that fits.

topup.description: PATCH only. Auto top-up of this key's limit from the account's credits; null clears it. The key needs a limit without limit_reset.

KeyTopup.description: When the key has less than below_usd of its limit left, the router raises the limit by add_usd, at most max_per_week_usd per UTC week (Monday to Sunday), and only while the account's available credits cover the key's remaining allowance after it. No money moves. It runs after a debit and when the key's limit would refuse a request. Each top-up, or skipped top-up with its reason, shows in Activity (kind topup) and the inbox. Rulebook caps still apply.

topups_this_week_usd.description: GET /api/v1/keys/{hash} and PATCH: the auto top-ups added to this key's limit since Monday 00:00 UTC.

kid.description: First 16 hex characters of SHA-256 of the raw key.

anchor.description: Where receipt roots are posted and which key signs them. Not signed: use it as your own configuration only when you fetched it yourself from the router's origin, and pin the first anchorer key.

network.description: The cluster's CAIP-2 id: solana:<first 32 characters of the genesis hash>. A verifier compares it with getGenesisHash of the RPC it uses.

program.description: Program mode: the trellis_anchor program id.

from_hour.description: Unix seconds on an hour boundary; 0 for the first key.

rotation_tx.description: The transaction in which the key before this one and this key signed trellis:anchorer:v1:<network>:<from hour>:<key>.

memo_v2_from_hour.description: Memo mode: root lines of this hour and later are v2 lines (trellis:root:v2:<network>:<hour>:<count>:<root>:<previous root's transaction, or 0>).

max_late_seconds.description: Memo mode: a root that lands later than this after its hour closed is late and is not an anchor.

fresh_within_ms.description: How old a verified attestation may be and still count as fresh.

attested.description: Runs that passed with hardware evidence (simulated evidence is not counted).

share.description: Covered part of the time the record spans within the window; null when nothing is recorded.

observed_ms.description: How much of the window the record spans.

history_complete.description: False when the record does not reach back to the start of the window; the earlier time is unknown, not covered and not uncovered.

buckets.description: Equal slices from the start of the window to now (48 for 24h, 84 for 7d): percent covered, or null before the record begins.

share.description: Covered part of the time the record spans within the window; null when nothing is recorded.

observed_ms.description: How much of the window the record spans.

history_complete.description: False when the record does not reach back to the start of the window; the earlier time is unknown, not covered and not uncovered.

buckets.description: Equal slices from the start of the window to now (48 for 24h, 84 for 7d): percent covered, or null before the record begins.

digests.description: Digests only: image_digest, compose_hash, model_digest, mrtd, rtmr0 to rtmr3, measurement.

from.description: Digests only: image_digest, compose_hash, model_digest, mrtd, rtmr0 to rtmr3, measurement.

to.description: Digests only: image_digest, compose_hash, model_digest, mrtd, rtmr0 to rtmr3, measurement.

probe.description: The latest health-probe outcome and when it began.

reason.description: A code from a fixed list with its message; never the provider's own text.

simulated.description: Development evidence: never counted as a fresh attestation.

tls_spki_sha256.description: SPKI hash of the certificate the connection was pinned to, when it was.

measurements.description: Digests only: image_digest, compose_hash, model_digest, mrtd, rtmr0 to rtmr3, measurement.

measurement_changed.description: The run's digests differ from the previous accepted run's, comparing the fields both report.

next.description: Pass as before for the next page; null on the last page.

verifiers.description: The verifiers that accepted the quote; empty unless status is attested.

policy_hash.description: The classifier policy hash this fresh attestation bound (the value sent as X-Trellis-Policy-Hash); null unless status is attested and one was bound.

measurement.description: Last recorded digests (image_digest, compose_hash, model_digest), status, attested_now, registers { mrtd, rtmr3 } of the recorded quote, transparency_log { found, inclusion_verified, checkpoint_signature_verified, subject (measurement_bundle or image_digest), entry_url, bundle, ... } and registry { address, state, tx_hash, registered_at }.

RouteExplanation.description: Versioned additive router statement, not an independent selection proof. eligible counts final-plan candidate offers before attempt limits for the serving model; skipped counts its exclusions. Fallback error classes cover earlier attempts, including earlier models, without raw errors or provider identities. No URLs, keys, addresses, content or weights. Both receipt signatures cover route.

decision_tag.description: The caller's X-Trellis-Decision-Tag, when DECISION_TAGS_ENABLED is true.

cost_details.description: The parts of the charge as USD decimal strings (upstream, royalty, margin and others).

over_hold.description: Present only when the provider reported usage priced above the hold: the list price of the reported usage, as a USD decimal string. The caller was charged the hold (payload.cost), never more, and the provider was paid no more than that.

payload.description: Signed fields. cost is what the caller was charged, which is never more than the hold taken before the call; cost_details.over_hold is present when a provider reported usage priced above that hold (on an encrypted chat receipt it is e2ee.over_hold). Optional route is a versioned additive claim when ROUTE_EXPLAIN_ENABLED is true (default false). Optional decision_tag is the caller-computed digest sent as X-Trellis-Decision-Tag (DECISION_TAGS_ENABLED, default false). Among them, disclosure (attested, policy or vendor-forwarded) and lane (public, attested or unlinkable) record how the call was served; attestation_simulated is true when the attestation behind an attested call is a development report. attestation_ref (see AttestationRef) is present on calls made under an attested council or attested dual verification. For a call paid with a blind token, payer is null and nullifier (the SHA-256 of the spent token) and token_key_id are present; nothing names an account. Receipts issued before these fields existed do not carry them.

privacy.description: The privacy label derived from payload for readers. It is not part of what is signed.

ReceiptV2.description: Receipt v2 (spec 0004 Section 4): a COSE_Sign1 over deterministic CBOR claims, signed EdDSA with the same key as v1 (kid is the key id's 8 bytes). claims is the JSON view of exactly what cose signs. Token counts are bucketed; nothing names a payer, an address or content.

leaf.description: sha256(sha256(COSE bytes)), as 0x and 64 hex characters.

chain.description: Streams only: the chunk hash chain head.

policy.description: Present only when the serving endpoint's fresh attestation bound a classifier policy.

cost_units.description: Amount charged in millionths of a US dollar, rounded up.

rid.description: The receipt id the sidecar gave it.

anchored.description: True only when the root was posted on chain and confirmed.

status.description: confirmed: on chain; pending: to be posted (the chain was unreachable); local: kept off chain because no chain is configured.

provider_id_hash.description: sha256 of the provider id's bytes: the providerId the root is posted under (trellis_anchor::post_host_root).

attestation_ref.description: 64 hex: SHA-256 of the boot quote the router verified, which every leaf in the root names.

receipt_key.description: The receipt key the quote binds; every leaf in the root verified under it.

proof.description: Sorted-pair sha256 Merkle path (node = sha256(min || max)) from the leaf to the root.

window.description: When the router collected the root's leaves: [from, to).

decision_tag.description: Optional: the SHA-256 of your order, computed on your side as the decision-receipt helpers do (canonical JSON, sha256:<64 hex>). The result reports decision_tag (the tag the receipt's signed contents carry, or null) and decision_tag_valid (whether it equals this value; null when omitted), and valid is false when they differ. Only the hash is sent.

Optional: the SHA-256 of your order, computed on your side as the decision-receipt helpers do (canonical JSON, sha256:<64 hex>). The result reports decision_tag (the tag the receipt's signed contents carry, or null) and decision_tag_valid (whether it equals this value; null when omitted), and valid is false when they differ. models.description: Catalog model ids in fallback order; no nested @route/.

provider.description: Provider preferences: order, only, ignore, allow_fallbacks, sort (price|latency|throughput), data_collection, zdr, require_parameters, max_price, and the privacy settings lane (public|attested) and disclosure (none|policy|any). For lane and disclosure the stricter of the route and the request applies, so a request can tighten a route but never loosen it; a route on the attested lane is served only by attested providers or refused. lane attested already implies disclosure none.

params.description: Default request parameters from a closed whitelist (temperature, top_p, top_k, min_p, top_a, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, repetition_penalty, max_tokens, seed, stop, reasoning, verbosity). Prompt fields are rejected.

model.description: Use as the request model, e.g. @route/my-coder.

allowed_models.description: Catalog ids or @route/<slug>; must be within the creator's allowlist.

metadata.description: Labels only, at most 2 KB; prompt-like keys are refused.

SpendReport.description: Spend for the caller's scope (a management key sees its account; other keys see themselves). UTC calendar.

HolderTier.description: One membership level. No field is an amount of money.

min.description: The threshold: the smallest balance that holds this tier, in whole tokens (decimal string). Holding more inside a tier adds nothing.

max_agent_keys.description: Active Agent Session keys per account, when higher than the standard limit; null leaves the standard limit.

max_saved_routes.description: Saved routes and presets per account, when higher than the standard limit; null leaves the standard limit.

max_batch_rows.description: Lines in one batch, when higher than the standard limit; null leaves the standard limit.

sealed_priority.description: Place in the sealed-lane admission queue when a host is full, and in Bushel purchase ordering; higher is served first, 0 is the standard place. A share of capacity is always kept for callers with no tier.

early_access_hours.description: How long before a newly listed model's early-access window ends this tier may use it.

vote_weight.description: The fixed weight of this tier's one vote in an advisory poll (0: no vote). Never the balance.

credits_never_expire.description: While a wallet holds this tier, the router sends no expiry notice or sweep for its key's credits.

badge.description: Whether an opted-in public agent profile may show the tier name.

challenge_digest.description: SHA-256 of the challenge, hex; the challenge_digest field of every token.

unit_price_usd.description: USD per token-unit for keys created from now on; each key states its own value_usd.

commitment.description: sha256(uint64be epoch || uint32be count || uint32be denominations[] || uint32be count || keyIds[]), the epoch commitment the issuer publishes; 0x and 64 hex characters.

value_usd.description: What one token of this key is worth; fixed for the key's life.

issued.description: Tokens signed with this key (a count).

keys.description: Oldest first; at most the latest 512.

key_id.description: The 8-bit key identifier: the epoch modulo 256.

entry_hash.description: SHA-256 chain: this entry committed to the one before it.

first_prev.description: The entry hash before the first key listed (64 zeros when the list starts at the first key ever).

key_id.description: A receipt signing key; see GET /api/v1/receipts/keys.

sig.description: Base64 Ed25519 signature over the canonical JSON of data.

key_id.description: Identifier of the credential this relay presents to the gateway.

independent.description: False when the relay's operator is the gateway's own operator.

chunked.description: Present only where the gateway accepts chunked Oblivious HTTP.

token_key_id.description: A key whose status is issuing.

items.description: 256 bytes, base64url: the blinded token input, below the key's modulus.

blinded_msgs.description: Distinct blinded messages, at most max_batch.

replayed.description: True when this exact purchase had already been made; nothing was charged again.

signatures.description: signatures[i] answers blinded_msgs[i]; 256 bytes each, base64url.

HolderStatus.description: The tier of the wallet behind the calling key and the perks that apply to the key now. A key that does not belong to a wallet sign-in account gets the same shape with wallet null and a hint.

enabled.description: Whether holder tiers run on this router.

wallet.description: The wallet behind this key (wallet sign-in keys only).

balance.description: Token balance in whole tokens (decimal string); null without a wallet or when it could not be read.

balance_error.description: True when the balance could not be read; no tier applies until it can.

next_tier.description: The next threshold above the balance; null at the top tier or when tiers are off.

remaining.description: How far the balance is below that threshold, in whole tokens.

limits.description: The limits this key runs under now. With no tier these are the standard limits.

tpm.description: Tokens per minute (0: no cap; null: not set on this key).

agent_keys.description: Active Agent Session keys per account (0: no cap).

hint.description: Present when the key has no wallet: how to see a tier.

input_tokens.description: Prompt tokens not read from or written to the provider's cache.

trellis.description: What the router says about the call.
The router's own error type (for example lane_unavailable), its metadata, and receipt_id when a refused call was billed.

ResponsesInputItem.description: An input item: a message, a function_call or custom_tool_call from an earlier turn, or the function_call_output or custom_tool_call_output for it.

role.description: developer is sent to the model as system.

output.description: The function's result: text, or input_text parts.

ResponsesRequest.description: A Responses API request. Options Trellis cannot honour because they need stored state are refused (store true, previous_response_id, conversation, background, prompt) and so is every tool that is not a function or custom tool.

model.description: Public model ID, as in chat completions.

max_output_tokens.description: Sent to the chat call as its output cap. The router always sends the provider an explicit cap: the smallest of this value, the catalog's output limit for the model (16,384 when the catalog has none) and the room the context leaves after the prompt bound; a higher value is clamped, not refused, and an omitted value is filled in.

format.description: text (default), json_object, or json_schema ({type, name, schema, strict, description}), sent as response_format. Requires a model and provider that support it.

reasoning.description: reasoning.effort is passed on as reasoning.effort; providers that do not support it drop it.

metadata.description: Echoed in the Response. Not sent to a provider.

user.description: Passed to the provider as the end-user identity, as in chat completions.

store.description: Must be false or omitted: Trellis stores no responses.

ResponsesObject.description: A Response. The request's instructions, tools, tool_choice, max_output_tokens, temperature, top_p, parallel_tool_calls, text, reasoning and user are echoed back; store is always false and previous_response_id null.

id.description: resp_ followed by the receipt id. There is nothing to fetch with it; the receipt is at GET /api/v1/receipts/{id} for the id without the resp_ prefix.

status.description: incomplete: the answer was cut off (incomplete_details.reason max_output_tokens or content_filter). failed appears only in a stream, in response.failed.

model.description: The model the router resolved the request to.

input.description: The freeform text the model gave the custom tool.

output.description: A message with output_text, and a function_call or custom_tool_call item for each tool call the model made.

cost.description: What the call cost in USD, as usage.cost in chat completions.

metadata.description: The request's metadata plus trellis_receipt_id (the id of the signed receipt), trellis_lane (public, attested or unlinkable), trellis_disclosure (the class the receipt records, once known) and trellis_policy_hash (only when the serving endpoint attested one).

RagRequest.description: Unknown fields are refused (400), so a misspelt option is never silently ignored. There is no cache option: the response cache is never used.

documents.description: The text to search: plain strings or {id, text}. At most 200 documents and 2 MiB of UTF-8 text by default (RAG_MAX_DOCUMENTS, RAG_MAX_BYTES). A string, or an object without id, is named doc-<position>, starting at 1. Ids must be unique; a document with no text is refused.

model.description: The chat model that writes the answer. An embedding model is refused.

embedding_model.description: The model that embeds the chunks and the question. Default: qwen/qwen3-embedding-8b if the catalog serves it, else the cheapest embedding model; models with an attested endpoint are considered first unless the request asks for a lane or ceiling, when only models that meet it are.

top_k.description: How many of the best chunks go into the prompt. A request whose largest possible prompt would not fit the chat model's context is refused (400 context_too_small) before anything is embedded.

chunk.description: Sizes are in characters (UTF-16 code units). A chunk ends at a paragraph, line or sentence boundary when there is one in its last 40%, otherwise at a space.

overlap.description: Characters shared by neighbouring chunks: at most half of size. Default: 15% of size.

include_excerpts.description: Return each source's text as excerpt. Off by default: the response then carries where each source lies (start, end) and never the text.

provider.description: The lane and disclosure ceiling, applied to every call. Other routing options are not accepted. If you send none, the lane pinned on the key (routing.provider) is used, and if there is none the router chooses (see the operation description).

lane.description: attested: every call goes only to a provider with attested retention and a fresh attestation the router verified; when one cannot be served the request is refused, never downgraded. unlinkable is not available here (400).

disclosure.description: Same as provider.disclosure on chat completions.

ref.description: The number of the source in the prompt, and in the citations ([1], [2]) the model was asked to make. Sources are in rank order.

chunk_index.description: Position of the chunk within its document, from 0.

score.description: Cosine similarity of the chunk's vector with the question's, rounded to 6 places.

end.description: The chunk is the document text from start to end (characters).

excerpt.description: The chunk's text. Present only when include_excerpts is true.

RagCall.description: One provider call, as its signed receipt records it. Read the receipt with GET /api/v1/receipts/{receipt_id}.

lane.description: The lane the call was made under.

disclosure.description: The class the call was served under, from its receipt.

inputs.description: Embeddings calls: how many texts (the question and chunks) the call embedded.

policy_hash.description: The classifier policy hash the serving endpoint attested, when it did (X-Trellis-Policy-Hash of that call).

upstream_attestation.description: For an attested gateway: what the router checked of the gateway's receipt for this call. attested is true only when the receipt shows an upstream the gateway verified inside a TEE.

withheld.description: The provider had answered, but the router withheld the reply because the receipt did not show an attested upstream. The call is billed; its signed receipt says why.

attestation_simulated.description: The attestation behind this call is a development report; a production router refuses those.

id.description: The chat call's receipt id: the same as X-Receipt-Id.

receipts.description: Every provider call the request made, in order: the embeddings calls, then the chat call.

lane.description: The lane every call was made under.

lane_source.description: request: you stated a lane or a disclosure ceiling (even public or any) and it was used as stated. default: you stated none, and the router chose attested when the chat model and the embedding model both have an attested endpoint, else public.

lane_note.description: Present when the default lane was public: which model had no known attested endpoint.

disclosure.description: The weakest class among all the calls, from their receipts; null when a call's class is not known.

attestation_simulated.description: Present when any call's attestation was a development report.

note.description: The signed note, as served at /tlog/checkpoint.

cosigned_by.description: Names of the configured witnesses whose cosignatures are attached.

witnessed.description: True when at least the quorum of configured witnesses cosigned.

rekor.description: Present only with Rekor anchoring on: this checkpoint's Rekor entry, or null until it is anchored.

origin.description: Checkpoint origin and the log's key name.

verifier_key.description: Signed-note verifier key <origin>+<key id>+<base64(0x01 || Ed25519 key)>.
<name>+<key id>+<base64(0x04 || Ed25519 key)>, a cosignature/v1 key.

witnessed_size.description: Tree size of the newest checkpoint the quorum cosigned.

rekor.description: Rekor anchoring (TLOG_REKOR_ENABLED): the same fields as GET /api/v1/tlog/rekor without the list; null when anchoring is off.

key_id.description: SHA-256 of the key's SubjectPublicKeyInfo, hex.

public_key_pem.description: The anchoring key, an ECDSA P-256 public key (PEM).

subject.description: The key id, epoch or provider the entry is about.

entry.description: The entry's canonical JSON; its leaf hash is SHA-256(0x00 || these bytes).
